# Principal Technical Marketing Engineer | UK | Remote
United Kingdom (Remote)
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
**The Opportunity:**
Grafana Labs is looking for a technically fluent engineer who loves building powerful demos, explaining complex systems clearly, and helping SRE and platform engineering leaders understand the value of our open approach to observability.
As Grafana’s offering shifts from dashboards to industry-leading agentic observability, our Product Marketing team is responsible for closing the gap between what our products can do and how customers understand that value. That means building clear, consistent positioning, enabling sellers with trustworthy technical narratives, and creating content that helps Platform Engineering teams quickly grasp why Grafana Cloud is the right choice for them.
As a Technical Product Marketer you will play a critical part in that transformation. You’ll be the hands-on engineer who brings our technical story to life for buyers, not just practitioners. You’ll build core demos, run technical workshops and webinars, and act as the technical bridge between our Product and Sales orgs. Your work will help SRE and platform engineering leaders evaluate Grafana with confidence, equip sales engineers with better tools and talk tracks, and ensure our technical value shows up clearly and consistently across the entire customer journey.
This is a unique chance to shape how Grafana tells its story as we evolve our positioning in the AI era, strengthen seller enablement, and build a repeatable system for communicating product value.
**What You'll Be Doing:**
**Build strategic, buyer-focused demos, videos, workshops, and webinars**
* Create and maintain polished, narrative-driven demos that highlight Grafana’s value for SRE and platform engineering leaders.
* Record high-quality technical demo videos and walkthroughs in partnership with our video and content teams.
* Lead webinars, workshops, and technical sessions designed for evaluators.
* Teach customers not just how Grafana works, but why our approach is differentiated and valuable.
* Use AI tools to generate variations, summaries, and reusable assets that scale technical content across channels.
**Enable Solutions (Sales) Engineers with clear, consistent technical storytelling**
* Serve as PMM’s technical liaison to the SE org, ensuring consistent messaging and demo guidance.
* Produce technical enablement assets, value-driven talk tracks, competitive narratives, and demo best practices.
* Help SEs and sellers communicate Grafana’s story with clarity, confidence, and differentiation.
**Collaborate with PMMs to drive technical buyer engagement across high-impact channels**
* Partner with PMMs to identify the most important buyer personas, problems, and technical messages, and help shape the content strategy needed to reach them.
* Extend technical narratives into impactful buyer-facing channels including analyst briefings (Gartner, Forrester), industry forums, podcasts, conferences, and online technical communities.
* Bring a technical perspective to PMM planning—helping ensure our content, campaigns, and enablement reflect the real challenges and priorities of SREs and engineering leaders.
**Use automation & AI to scale technical content**
* Partner with software engineers to streamline demo setup, content workflows, and asset updates through workflows, agents, scripts, and AI-driven tools.
* Use automation to make technical content more repeatable, discoverable, and scalable across teams.
**What Makes You a Great Fit:**
* 5+ years in a technical role (solutions engineering, SRE, DevOps, backend engineering, technical PMM, or similar).
* Interest and ability to travel to training and customer events 10-12 weeks per year.
* Strong understanding of observability concepts and the needs of SRE/platform teams.
* Ability to translate deep technical concepts into clear, value-focused stories.
* Experience presenting technical content through demos, workshops, or webinars.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, with a crisp, structured, persuasive style.
* Strong cross-functional collaboration; comfort working with PMM, Product, SEs, DevRel, and Field Engineering.
* High ownership mindset with the ability to drive projects from concept to completion.
* Comfort with light scripting or workflow automation.
**Bonus Points For:**
* Hands-on experience with Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Mimir, Tempo, or similar observability tools, or a background in Observability or Platform Engineering.
* Prior experience in Sales Engineering, DevRel, or technical product marketing.
* Familiarity with demo environment automation or infrastructure-as-code tools.
* Exceptional live presentation or workshop facilitation skills.
**Compensation & Rewards:**
In the UK, the base compensation range for this role is GBP 103,958- GBP 124,750. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.
*\*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.*
**Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:**
* **100% Remote, Global Culture -**As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
* **Scaling Organization** – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
* **Transparent Communication** – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
* **Innovation-Driven** – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
* **Open Source Roots** – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
* **Empowered Teams** – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
* **Career Growth Pathways** – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
* **Approachable Leadership** – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
* **Passionate People** – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
* **In-Person onboarding** - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
* **Balance is Key** - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *\*We will comply with local legislation where applicable.*

You hold the single accurate view of who is working on what across EMEA, decide how work gets covered when capacity runs out, and are the person the business comes to before it commits to anything new. You run the weekly resourcing rhythm, keep Paprika accurate, and bring in freelance support when the permanent team can't absorb the work.
This is not a coordination role. You make calls, hold others to the process, and are expected to say no with a reason.
What You'll Do
The weekly resourcing rhythm and Paprika
* Chair the weekly resource meeting. Run the department-by-department capacity review off the Strategic Time Viewer, resolve what can be resolved in the room, and drive actions to close afterwards.
* Attend the weekly Incoming meeting for early sight of new briefs, pitches and upcoming work. Take the casting requirements and pipeline changes from it and turn them into bookings.
* Keep jobs in Paprika accurate and current. Create internal and pitch jobs to the naming convention, keep pipeline stages honest, chase stale jobs to a decision, and close what's dead.
* Keep the schedule clean and complete - everything on the system, including non-billable, pitch and internal work, with clashes and expired retainers removed and leave reflected.
* Know at any point what's firm and what's speculative. Pencilled and pipeline work is visible as such, confidence states are applied consistently, and you can say what's real without having to ask.
* Hold a clear view of business priorities, so when speculative work collides with committed work, you know which one gives, and why.
* Hold PMs and client services to the booking rules. Bookings are clean before the meeting, not during it.
* Act as the point of contact for resourcing across the business, including requests that arrive without a PM attached.
Freelance resourcing
* Identify freelance need early, usually at pre-sale and before the PM community is aware of it.
* Agree with the department head, and the PM where one is running the brief, whether a gap is filled by freelance, absorbed internally, or pushed back on timings.
* Brief the Talent team on what's needed and by when: skill, level, duration and budget. Talent find the people; you define the requirement and confirm the fit against the plan.
* Make sure freelancers are set up, booked and visible in the schedule, and see the cover through to completion. PMs commission directly on their own briefs; you keep the overall picture straight across all of it.
* Track freelance spend against budget across the region, and report where it's going and why.
* Keep the freelance tracker current as the live record of who's on, where, and at what cost.
Onboarding, training and compliance
* Onboard every new starter on timesheets, Paprika and how resourcing works here. Finance create the Paprika record; you check the set-up is right, including that the person is bookable with a utilisation target in place.
* Own weekly timesheet compliance for EMEA, including the escalation process, and report repeat offenders to their department head.
* Train PMs and client services on the booking rules, and keep the supporting guidance current.
* Make sure leavers are cleared from the schedule so reporting stays accurate.
Resource data and system integrity
* Check that percentage utilisation is set for every person, contract end dates are correct, and grades and rates are right - chase Finance where they're not. Without this, every capacity and cost report the agency produces is wrong.
* Maintain the saved views and the ready reckoner of billable targets as people and contracts change.
* Flag system issues and development needs to the Operations Director, who owns Paprika.
Improving how it works
* Look for efficiencies and better ways of running resourcing, and put them in place rather than proposing them and waiting to be told.
* Use the tools available, including AI, to take manual effort out of reporting, reconciliation and meeting follow-up.
* Keep the resourcing guidance and documentation current, so the process holds when people are away.
Decisions You Own
*(Taken with input from the relevant department head - consultation is expected, waiting for their decision is not.)*
* Who gets booked where when two departments want the same person.
* Whether a gap is filled by freelance, agreed with the department head.
* When work must be re-planned or turned down due to capacity, with the reason recorded.
* Whether a department's bookings are good enough to pass review.
* When a compliance issue becomes a performance conversation.
What You Escalate
* Freelance spend above the agreed threshold.
* Client commitments already made that the schedule can't support.
* Headcount - you build the case, the decision sits above you.
* Structural change to the resourcing process itself.
About You
Experience
* 3-5 years of resourcing or studio traffic in a busy agency, running a mix of project work and retained accounts with multiple competing demands. You've run traffic properly and can point to it.
* Casting judgement - matching the right person to the work on skill, level and fit, rather than filling a slot with whoever's free. This is the part of the job we care most about.
* The judgement to prioritise between competing demands, and the confidence to explain a decision to someone who didn't get what they asked for.
* A track record of briefing and managing freelance resource, and of managing a budget rather than just reporting on it.
* Experience holding senior people to a process, and improving processes that aren't working.
* Confident working in a resourcing and job management system. Experience with Paprika is useful but not essential - we can teach the system.
* Comfortable with data. You can read a capacity report, spot what's wrong with it, and explain it to someone who doesn't want to hear it.
* You use AI in your work already, or you're ready to learn quickly. A good part of this role is reporting, reconciliation and follow-up, and we expect it done with the tools available rather than by hand. Greenpark has been building AI into how we work since 2022, and everyone here is expected to keep pace with it.
Who You Work With
The role reports to the Operations Director. You'll also work closely with the Head of Delivery and Head of Client Services, and from there with the department heads across SEO, Content, Creative and Strategy, and the PM community.
* Operations Director. Your line manager and escalation point for capacity decisions and process issues.
* Head of Delivery. Delivery priorities, PM capacity, and project pace.
* Head of Client Services. What's coming in, what's been committed to clients, and where the pipeline is heading.
* Department heads. Capacity, skills and the right person for a piece of work. You'll challenge each other - that's the point.
* Project managers. Day-to-day bookings, accuracy, freelance briefs, and holding the booking rules.
* Talent team. Source freelance and permanent candidates against the requirements you set.
At Greenpark, we believe the best ideas come from the widest range of perspectives.

## Job description
**About the role:**
Greyparrot builds AI-powered waste analytics — software that identifies and quantifies material streams in real time, delivered through analysers we design and manufacture. Hardware and software are equally core to the product: the analysers exist to feed the software, and the software is only as good as hardware that ships on time, works reliably, and scales with demand.
We are moving out of an R&D-volume phase into steady, operationalised production — roughly 150 units built in 2026, with 2027 volumes forecast at 500+. Analysers are built by a production partner based in Wales, using parts sourced from Asia & Europe, and shipped to customers across the US, Europe, and the UK. Right now, production ownership is split: forecasting and budget approval sit with the COO, while purchasing, including placing parts orders and fielding supplier and production-partner queries, has defaulted to the Hardware Manager, who knows the suppliers best but needs to return to R&D. Neither is a dedicated supply chain role, which makes this a function that can't scale independently of either of them.
This role exists to take that ownership on properly: the production partner relationship, the parts pipeline that feeds it, the ERP that tracks all of it, and the supplier and freight relationships that determine what it costs, including outbound and returns flows. Stock and order tracking is manual today, and a first version of the ERP will be stood up before you start. You take it over from day one and own it from there: what it holds, how well it fits, and how it grows with volume. This role sits alongside the Logistics & Delivery Lead, who owns shipment booking, last-mile delivery, and on-site installation. This role owns carrier contracts and rates, customs, and returns, plus the planning, forecasting, and partner management that everything downstream depends on, and the handover between the two is explicit.
**Mission**
*To ensure Greyparrot always has the analysers, parts, and shipping capacity to meet demand - on time, at a defensible cost - as production scales from early stage volumes into growth scale.*
**Outcomes**
These are the results you will be held to. How you achieve them is yours to figure out.
* **Production and stock are actively managed, not tracked after the fact.** Iota’s build schedule, work-in-progress, and finished-goods stock are managed against real, current demand — the business is never caught short of analysers to ship, and never sitting on cash tied up in stock it doesn’t need yet. Stock is held within Iota’s holding limit (currently around 50 units), with a third-party logistics provider (3PL) for anything that needs to sit beyond it.
* **Parts arrive before they’re needed, not when they’re missed.** Global parts orders — mostly from Asia — are placed against a rolling forecast that respects real lead times (currently around 18 weeks), so a line ramp or a demand spike never stalls production because an order went in too late. Orders within the agreed purchasing budget are yours to approve; only spend above it goes to the COO.
* **Capacity is a known number, not a guess.** Production capacity — build rate, ramp time, and refurbishment throughput — is forecast against the sales pipeline and board targets, so Operations and Commercial always know what can actually be built and shipped, and by when, without needing to ask.
* **Stock, orders, and production status are visible across the business, in a system you own.** You own the ERP that replaces today’s manual tracking — its requirements, configuration, data quality, adoption, and ongoing administration, and the roadmap for it as volume grows — so the current picture of parts, stock, and production is visible to whoever needs it, whenever they need it.
* **Supplier economics are actively managed, not accepted as given.** Rates with the parts suppliers and shipping providers are benchmarked and renegotiated on a regular cycle, keeping landed cost per unit under control as volume scales.
* **Commercial demand drives purchasing only when it’s firm.** Forecasts and reserves from Commercial turn into purchase orders and dispatch only once there is a signed contract and a completed site-readiness form, so parts and units aren’t committed against demand that doesn’t land.
* **Product version changes land cleanly.** When a new analyser version or bill of materials replaces the current one, the cutover is planned across parts, stock, and Iota’s build schedule, so old-version parts aren’t left stranded and the new version isn’t held up waiting for them.
* **Returned and refurbished units flow back into supply deliberately.** Returned units are tracked, assessed, and either refurbished and restocked or retired, with their costs and customs treatment accounted for, so the refurbishment stream adds supply rather than confusion.
* **Outbound logistics is reliable in every market we ship to.** Shipments to the US, Europe, and UK are planned and executed to account for each region’s customs, duties, and documentation requirements, so delivery timelines hold and nothing gets stuck at a border; returns are tracked against outbound shipments so customs and duties reconcile.
* **A single point of failure doesn’t stay a single point of failure.** The risk of relying on one production partner and long parts lead times is named explicitly, with real mitigations in place — buffer stock, an escalation path, and a live plan to qualify a second production partner (likely US-based) so the business isn’t exposed to one site, one region, or one relationship.
* **Hardware, Finance, and Commercial all work from the same picture.** Production status, capacity constraints, and cost data are visible and current for the teams that plan around them, without each function needing a separate update. And, Hardware's time goes to R&D, not purchasing or supplier calls.
**Competencies**
How you work matters as much as what you deliver. These reflect Greyparrot's values, at Senior IC tier.
**CURIOSITY**
You build a culture of asking why in the supply chain — why a forecast missed, why a part slipped, why a supplier's price moved — and you encourage Hardware, Finance, and Commercial to ask the same of you. You're willing to be wrong and to update your view publicly when new evidence warrants it, whether that's a supplier, a forecast, or how the ERP is set up, and you share your reasoning where others can see it.
**CUSTOMER CHAMPION**
You encourage the people around you to put the customer at the centre of production and purchasing calls, not as an afterthought. You translate customer and demand signals into forecasting, ordering, and capacity decisions the team can act on, and you translate operational reality — what can be built and shipped, and by when — back to Commercial in terms they can take to a customer.
**IMPACT**
You take on the higher-ambiguity work — the ERP, a second production partner, a forecast that has to hold at 500+ units — not only the convenient pieces. You state outcomes, not outputs: what changed in cost, lead time, stock accuracy, or capacity because of your work, published where the company can read it, including when it didn't land. You summarise a problem, your recommendation, and the trade-offs concisely so decisions can be made quickly.
**AGILITY**
You review and improve processes, routines, and tools when they've stopped fitting purpose — manual tracking, ordering rhythms, forecasting cadence. You make decisions in ambiguity — a demand spike, a delayed part, a product version cutover — without pushing uncertainty up or sideways, and you document the trigger, the decision, and the trade-offs. You run changes as tests and share what you learned openly, including when it didn't work.
**INTEGRITY**
You make decisions in public forums, not private channels, and you name what you're holding back and why. You hold peers accountable to commitments in the moment — a forecast sign-off, a delivery date, a handover — and give candid feedback regularly rather than saving it up. You make it safe to flag a missed order, a bad forecast, or a supplier problem early, so it isn't buried.

* Has owned a supply chain, procurement, or production planning function end-to-end — not just executed within one — and is comfortable being the senior authority on production, parts, and logistics calls day-to-day, without escalating routine decisions upward.

* Has worked with third-party logistics providers (3PLs) — contracting them and managing stock held with them against a holding limit, including inventory reporting and reconciliation.
* Comfortable with long-lead-time, capacity-constrained components (electronics, custom hardware) and the forecasting discipline that requires.
* Understands customs, duties, and international shipping documentation (Incoterms, HS codes) for outbound freight to the US, EU, and UK.
* Commercially literate: can read a landed-cost breakdown, model unit economics, and negotiate from an understanding of true cost drivers, not just headline price.
* Comfortable building process from scratch with a small internal team and a single production partner, rather than inheriting an established function.

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

We're building the AI operations platform that finishes that work: AI agents that execute end-to-end processes across UIs and APIs, with governance built in.
We're a Series A company of around 70 people, freshly funded and expanding from Europe into the US. Our customers are large enterprise retailers and CPG brands, and the work we do with them shows up on the P&L.
## The role
As a **Senior Transformation Strategist**, you sit with a customer's executives and the people who actually do the work, find where value is trapped, size it, and turn it into a roadmap our platform delivers against. Think of it as consulting with a product behind you and a number at the end of every cycle.
This is a hands-on, individual-contributor seat. You'll structure messy problems fast, commit to a number with incomplete data, and tell a VP or COO what to do next, then do it again on the next workflow.
## What you'll do
* **Find and size the opportunity:** work through real operational data (spend, invoices, rate cards, SKUs) to build a baseline, make your assumptions explicit, and land on a number a CFO would forward.
* **Decide what's worth building:** rank the next workflows by size, frequency and capturable value before asking whether we can build them.
* **Own the executive relationship:** be the direct counterpart to COOs, CFOs and operations leaders, run the follow-on conversations yourself, and tell clients what they need to hear even when it's uncomfortable.
* **Drive adoption on the ground:** spend real time with frontline teams so the change actually lands, and earn credibility with the people whose work is changing.
* **Expand the account:** turn a first proven workflow into the next five, and the next phase of the engagement.
* **Shape the function:** we're early, so you'll help define how this work is done here.
## What you bring
* **Top-tier consulting training,** ideally entering at analyst or post-MBA associate level, with **two or more years at Engagement Manager, Project Leader or Principal level** where you owned a workstream and faced the client without a partner in the room.
* **Short, high-stakes problem-solving cycles:** due diligence, value creation, portfolio operations or performance improvement work where you owned a number in revenue, margin, cost or working capital.
* **Top-down communication:** you lead with the point, support it with structure, and can do mental maths under time pressure.
* **Range across problem types:** you've solved more than one shape of problem (e.g. strategy and operations, diligence and delivery, or building something from zero).
* **A builder's streak:** something you've built outside work with a URL, a product with users, a startup or an operating role. You use AI tools daily and can explain why you choose one model over another.
* **Comfort with ambiguity:** you're energised by a Series A environment with no fixed playbook.
**Bonus:** retail, grocery or CPG exposure (category, trading, merchandising, supply chain), or PE-backed portfolio work. P&L ownership is **not** required; having sat with the people who do the work matters more.
## Logistics & what we offer
* **Location:** London. Expect three to four days a week on client site.
* **Compensation:** £130-160k all-in, plus equity.
* Real enterprise customers whose feedback drives what gets built next.
* Unlimited AI budget and a team that values ownership, pace and candour.
## How we hire
1. **Intro call** with our recruitment team.
2. **Live case (1 hour, no prep):** a real operational engagement with messy data. You'll be asked to structure the problem, do the maths live and close with a recommendation to an operations executive. Expect a meaningful quantitative component.
3. **Competency conversation (60-75 min, two interviewers):** change and adoption, business-value discipline, executive communication, judgment and AI-native working.
4. **Founder conversation** where relevant.
We aim to move from first contact to offer within about 25 days.

# VP of Engineering, Full Stack (CTO Track)
## About the company
We're a frontier AI lab building our own foundation model for safety-critical embedded control software. Think motor controllers, battery management, power electronics and vehicle systems, where a bug is a physical failure, not a 500 error.
Our platform puts that model to work. Its user-facing product is the environment where control engineers specify, generate, review, test and trace embedded software with AI assistance.
Our foundation model is available now. The job is to integrate it into the product and turn it into something engineers trust, on an architecture that takes each new model release without a rewrite.
## The role
You'll be the most senior engineer on the product and the person who decides how it's built. This is a hands-on role: you'll write a large share of the code in year one.
As the product and team grow, you'll grow into technical leadership of the platform, setting architecture, engineering standards and hiring. For the right person, this is a **clear path to CTO**.
You'll work directly with the founding team and the model research team. The bridge between a frontier model and a product that safety-critical engineers rely on runs through you.
**Reports to:** Founders
## What you'll do
* **Architecture:** Own the architecture across frontend, backend, data and infrastructure, and make the build-vs-buy calls.
* **Product delivery:** Ship features fast, working closely with product and early users who are control and embedded engineers.
* **Model integration:** Design the integration layer (inference serving, prompt and context management, tool use, streaming, evaluation hooks and fallbacks) so we integrate our model now and adopt future releases without a rewrite.
* **Trust workflows:** Build what engineers need to trust AI-generated code: traceability from requirements to code, diffing and review, test execution and audit trails.
* **Engineering foundations:** Set up CI/CD, observability, security, access control and cost control for GPU-backed workloads.
* **Enterprise readiness:** Prepare the product for enterprise customers in regulated industries: SSO, data isolation, on-prem or private-cloud deployment.
* **Team:** Hire, mentor and lead the first engineers, and define how the team works.
## What you bring
* 10+ years building and shipping production software, with real depth on both frontend and backend
* Strong TypeScript and React (or equivalent modern frontend), plus at least one backend language such as Python, Go or TypeScript/Node
* Experience as the founding, lead or principal engineer on a product taken from early stage to paying customers
* Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered features in production: model APIs or self-hosted inference, streaming, evaluation and cost/latency trade-offs
* Solid cloud and infrastructure skills (AWS, GCP or Azure; containers; infrastructure as code)
* Good architectural judgement: you know when to move fast and when the cost of a shortcut is too high
* Experience hiring and leading engineers, or a clear appetite to do so
* Clear written and spoken English, and comfort working directly with founders, researchers and customers
### Nice to have
* Familiarity with safety and quality standards such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or FedRAMP
* Experience building developer tools, IDEs, code editors (e.g. Monaco, VS Code extensions) or code analysis tooling
* Experience serving custom or fine-tuned models (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton or similar) and GPU infrastructure
* Rust or C/C++ experience
* Experience selling to and deploying in regulated or security-conscious enterprises
## What we offer
* CTO-level ownership of a product at the meeting point of frontier AI and real-world engineering
* A clear path to CTO as the company grows
* Competitive salary and meaningful CTO-level equity
* Direct work with a founding team that combines AI research with hands-on experience building high-voltage and electric drive systems
* London office with hybrid working; remote considered for exceptional candidates
* A full benefits package
## Logistics
* **Location:** London preferred (hybrid); exceptional candidates considered globally
* **Type:** Full-time, permanent

## About GV Health
We are a science and technology-driven company focused on creating safer environments for human health. Through innovation, education, and integrated solutions, we address the challenges of infection prevention, environmental hygiene, and sustainability in healthcare worldwide.
Our customers include NHS Trusts, Independent Healthcare Providers, Facilities Management organisations, and Integrated Care Systems. Through evidence-led solutions and long-term partnerships, we help healthcare organisations improve outcomes, reduce risk, and support operational excellence.
## Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced and commercially driven Key Account Manager to lead the development of some of GV Health’s most strategically important healthcare accounts.
This is a senior sales role focused on managing and growing relationships across NHS Trusts, Facilities Management providers, Integrated Care Boards (ICBs), and wider Integrated Care Systems (ICSs). The successful candidate will be responsible for developing long-term account strategies, influencing key stakeholders, identifying growth opportunities, and delivering profitable revenue growth across a complex healthcare landscape.
Unlike traditional sales roles, success in this position requires the ability to navigate multiple decision-makers, understand system-level healthcare priorities, and build credibility with both operational and executive stakeholders.
This role provides the opportunity to take ownership of an established portfolio of strategic healthcare accounts while joining a business with ambitious UK and international growth plans.
We are seeking someone who can make an immediate impact but is equally excited by the prospect of growing with the organisation over the longer term. As GV Health continues to expand, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to broaden their remit into areas such as strategic distributor management, export and international markets, key account leadership, and wider commercial development initiatives.
We are therefore looking for an adaptable, commercially minded professional who is comfortable operating in a dynamic environment where responsibilities may evolve alongside business growth and individual strengths.
The ideal candidate will combine strong commercial acumen with exceptional relationship-building skills and a proven track record of successfully managing and growing strategic healthcare accounts.

### Strategic Account Management
* Develop and execute comprehensive account plans for key NHS, FM, and healthcare system accounts.
* Build long-term partnerships with senior stakeholders across healthcare organisations, ensuring GV Health becomes a trusted strategic partner.
* Identify, qualify, and develop opportunities for account growth within existing and prospective strategic accounts.

* Lead pricing discussions, contract negotiations, and commercial proposals.
* Monitor account profitability and margin performance, identifying opportunities for improvement.
* Collaborate with internal stakeholders to develop customer-specific growth strategies and business cases.

* Lead tender engagement from opportunity identification through to contract award.
* Work closely with commercial, technical, and compliance teams to ensure high-quality submissions.
* Ensure tender responses are commercially robust, compliant, and submitted within deadlines.

# Product Compliance Officer
Role Specification
## Introduction
A great opportunity for a professional from a product regulatory compliance background with scientific understanding to join a successful technical department in a thriving international science and technology company.
The company provides infection prevention and control solutions to the healthcare sector, with a focus on environmental hygiene and hazardous waste management products. Products include disinfectants, cleaners, decontamination systems, waste bags and protective clothing.
This role offers unique opportunities for professional development and career advancement, building a highly transferable skill set across a diverse range of products.
The company has grown rapidly over the last 30 years, providing key support to the NHS during the COVID-19 pandemic and releasing various groundbreaking technologies since.
The regulatory landscape in the healthcare sector is evolving rapidly due to changes in sustainability and global supply chains, creating the ideal space for an individual seeking an exciting new challenge and accelerated career path.

# Social Content Producer - B2B experience Required (London based)
## Turn bold ideas into content people want to watch. Shape HowNow’s voice across video, social, podcasts and product stories while building the future of learning.
We usually respond within three days
Our mission is to make meaningful learning a part of your everyday 🧠. The shelf life of our skills is now less than 5 years. So, if you stopped learning today, your skills would soon be irrelevant. Think that’s a big problem? You’d be right.
Enter HowNow. Founded in 2019, our Learning and Skills Platform is disrupting the way people learn and upskill through technology. Whether it's finding a quick answer, learning skills or tapping into shared knowledge, we make it easy for people to learn what they need, when they need it.
Already used by fast-growing scale-ups and global enterprises, such as Trainline, Depop and Sanofi, we’re pushing the boundaries of how people learn.
Hi, I'm Duncan, Head of GTM at HowNow 👋🏾. I'm hiring a Social Content Producer. It's a genuinely exciting time to be here: we've just been recognised on the 2026 Fosway 9-Grid for Learning Systems; we shipped Guru (our AI workplace coach), and it's already live with customers; and we're now working with brands like Trainline, TomTom, Investec, Depop across more than 30 countries.
Alongside the opportunities to develop and grow your career, we're a fun and friendly bunch.
**The role**
This is a B2B content role for a true maker. We don't want traditional, polished corporate content, but you must understand how to engage smart, busy professionals and B2B buyers on LinkedIn.
Someone who can spot an interesting idea, figure out how to tell it, pick up a camera, shoot it, edit it, design around it, and turn it into something people actually want to watch.
Our audience consists of smart, busy HR, L&D, and business leaders who have seen every 'future of work' post going. Your challenge is translating complex B2B SaaS concepts into compelling stories for them.
You'll create for LinkedIn first (it's where our buyers and community live), plus Instagram and YouTube, including:
* Short-form social and founder-led video
* Product stories, demos and launches
* The L&D Disrupt podcast: clips, interviews and guest moments
* YouTube and longer-form video
* Carousels, graphics and social visuals
* Motion graphics and animations
* Event and reactive content
* New formats we haven't thought of yet
Sometimes it'll be beautifully produced. Sometimes the right answer will be an iPhone, a great idea, and 30 minutes.
Knowing the difference is part of the job.
**Day-to-day tasks will include 📩**
**Find the story.** Work with our founder, product and go-to-market (GTM) teams to turn rough ideas, conversations, new products, customer wins, and what's happening in AI and work into great creative.
**Shoot.** Founder content, podcasts, interviews, events, and whatever else the idea needs. You'll understand framing, lighting, and sound without needing a production crew.
**Edit.** This should be one of your superpowers. You understand hooks, pacing, cuts, captions, sound, and what makes someone keep watching.
**Design.** Create great-looking carousels, graphics, thumbnails, product visuals, and other social content. Work within our brand and help it evolve as needed.
**Make our products interesting.** Don't give us another “5 new features” video. You need the B2B acumen to understand what actually solves a problem for our software buyers. Whether it's Guru, our AI agent, or something the team shipped last week, find the product moment that makes an HR leader think, “Wait. How did it do that?”
**Build formats people recognise.** Help us develop recurring series, visual styles, and creative formats that become recognisably HowNow.
**Test, measure, learn.** Try things, see what lands, and double down. You'll own the numbers for what you make (reach, engagement, saves, shares, follower growth) and use them to decide what we make next.
**Shape the strategy.** Bring ideas, not just execution. Stay close to how LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube are changing, and help decide where and how we show up.
**Make great organic work harder.** Turn our best-performing organic content into ad-ready versions for paid social.
**Keep the engine running.** Juggle several projects at once and ship on a steady weekly rhythm without letting quality slip.
**The key things that we will be looking for in applicants 🔑**
Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We'd rather see what you can make.
* You can take an idea from concept to finished piece yourself
* You're excellent at shooting and editing video in Premiere Pro, Final Cut, or similar, with After Effects or similar for motion
* You have strong visual and design skills, and you're at home in Photoshop, Illustrator, and Lightroom or similar (plus Figma and Canva when speed matters)

I'm looking for a technically strong Financial Crime Data Lead to take ownership of the data engineering capability supporting financial crime operations within a leading UK financial services organisation. **Deep, hands-on expertise in both Snowflake and dbt is absolutely essential for this position.**
This isn't a purely strategic or people management role. I'm looking for someone who has significant experience designing, building and optimising production data platforms using both technologies, and who can set the technical direction whilst remaining close to the engineering. The role offers the opportunity to build a trusted financial crime data foundation, bringing together information across transaction monitoring, screening, onboarding, CRM and operational systems to improve data quality, regulatory controls, reporting and future AI capabilities
### The role
You'll take technical ownership of the financial crime data platform, shaping its architecture, engineering standards and delivery whilst leading a focused data engineering capability. Key responsibilities include:
* Snowflake architecture and engineering: Own the design, implementation and optimisation of Snowflake environments, including warehouse architecture, schema design, performance tuning, security, access controls and cost optimisation.
* dbt development and architecture: Establish and develop robust dbt transformation frameworks, including complex SQL models, incremental processing, macros, testing, documentation, lineage and CI/CD integration.
* Hands-on data engineering: Design and build production-grade SQL and Python pipelines, integrating data from multiple internal and external platforms.
* Data modelling: Develop scalable data models covering clients, entities, transactions, alerts, screening outcomes, risk ratings, investigations and audit records.
* Data quality and governance: Establish automated testing, reconciliation, data lineage, monitoring and governance controls across sensitive financial crime datasets.
* Technical leadership: Define engineering standards, review architectural decisions, mentor engineers and ensure delivery follows strong software engineering practices.
* Financial crime integration: Bring together data from AML, KYC, transaction monitoring, screening, CRM and other operational systems.
* AI and automation: Build reliable, well-governed datasets that support future machine learning, anomaly detection, alert optimisation and investigation automation.
### What I'm looking for
The most important requirement is someone with **genuine technical depth across Snowflake and dbt**, backed by strong SQL/Python engineering and experience leading data platform delivery. **Essential experience:**
* Extensive, hands-on Snowflake engineering experience, including architecture, data modelling, performance optimisation, warehouse management, security and cost control.
* Advanced dbt expertise, having designed and developed production transformation frameworks rather than simply worked with existing models.
* Strong SQL skills, including complex transformations, query optimisation, data quality checks, reconciliation and scalable modelling techniques.
* Strong Python engineering capabilities for pipelines, automation, API integrations, testing and reusable data processing.
* Experience designing and delivering modern cloud data platforms in complex enterprise environments.
* Strong understanding of data engineering best practices, including Git, CI/CD, automated testing, observability and production support.
* Previous experience leading engineers, setting technical standards and taking ownership of architecture and delivery.
* Experience working with sensitive, governed data in financial services or another highly regulated environment.
**Particularly interesting experience:**
* Financial crime, AML, KYC, sanctions screening or transaction monitoring data.
* Integrating financial crime platforms, CRM systems and third-party vendor APIs.
* Data Vault, dimensional modelling or complex entity resolution.
* Building data foundations for machine learning, anomaly detection or GenAI applications.
* Experience with Azure Data Factory, Airflow or similar orchestration technologies.
### Why consider it?
This is an opportunity to take genuine technical ownership of an important data engineering capability, rather than inherit an established platform with limited scope to influence its direction. You'll help shape how financial crime data is structured, integrated, governed and consumed across the organisation, with the opportunity to introduce engineering standards, improve operational processes and enable future automation and AI use cases. The role offers a combination of hands-on technical challenges, architectural ownership, leadership responsibilities and direct exposure to senior business and technology stakeholders. **Package:**
Up to £120,000 base salary, plus bonus, excellent pension and wider benefits. **Location:**
London, Glasgow or Liverpool, with hybrid working. London-based employees attend the office 2–3 days per week. If you're a senior Data Engineer, Principal Data Engineer or Data Engineering Lead with substantial Snowflake and dbt experience, and you're interested in taking ownership of a business-critical data platform, I'd be keen to have a conversation.

IDEMIA Secure Transactions, a division of IDEMIA Group, is the leading technology provider making it safer and easier to pay and connect. The Operations Contract Manager is a global strategic role responsible for driving contract management excellence, business transformation, and contract lifecycle governance across IDEMIA Secure Transactions' Payment Services Business Unit. Operating across regions and functions, the role supports the transformation of contract management into a consistent, scalable, and business-enabling capability that strengthens operational performance, mitigates risk, and protects contractual value throughout the customer lifecycle.

The role plays a key part in enabling global business transformation initiatives by establishing governance disciplines, driving process improvement, increasing contractual visibility, and supporting the operationalisation of strategic and high-risk customer agreements. Working across a diverse global stakeholder network, the Operations Contract Manager collaborates closely with Sales, Legal, Finance, Delivery, Operations, Customer Success, Program Management, and senior leadership teams to ensure alignment between contractual commitments, business objectives, and operational execution. While operating within the accountability framework defined by the Contract Management operating model, the role serves as a catalyst for continuous improvement, business excellence, and transformational change.
Through strong stakeholder engagement and disciplined governance, the Operations Contract Manager helps embed sustainable and scalable operating practices, improve decision-making through enhanced contract visibility, reduce operational leakage, strengthen risk management, and support the successful delivery of strategic business transformation objectives across the global organization
## **Key Missions**
**Business Excellence and Contract Operations Transformation** • Define and support the transformation roadmap for Contract Management and related business excellence initiatives, aligned with IST’s global strategic priorities and BU operating model expectations. • Shape the as-is / to-be vision by assessing current regional practices, designing target ways of working, and supporting transition plans that improve consistency, efficiency, and control. • Drive digital enablement including Salesforce integration, CLM, repositories, dashboards, and workflow industrialization to reduce cycle time and strengthen transparency for decision-makers. • Lead change management across Legal, Contract Management, Sales, Finance, Delivery, Operations, and regional teams to ensure adoption, manage resistance, and embed continuous improvement. • Define and monitor KPIs and dashboards linking contract operations performance to measurable business outcomes, including efficiency, risk mitigation, contract visibility, and customer satisfaction.
• Prepare regular reporting for senior leadership on contract status, portfolio risks, leakage exposure, governance performance, and improvement actions.
**Contract operations and governance** • Support controlled contract lifecycle governance by reinforcing contractual visibility, governance routines, obligation monitoring, and lifecycle discipline for strategic and high-risk projects. • Contribute to pre-signature readiness where engaged by supporting commercial structuring within approved parameters, identifying contractual risk areas, and ensuring appropriate SME coordination. • Manage post-execution governance activities including contractual milestone monitoring, action tracking, early warning alerts, escalation preparation, and governance meeting support and lessons learned. • Coordinate complex Change Requests end-to-end for updated or new scope, ensuring documentation, SME consultation, commercial decision support, approval tracking, and amendment preparation are completed in line with the operating model.
• Support amendment, renewal, and close-out activities by contributing to renewal preparation, critical deal reviews, contract close-out, and return-on-experience capture.
• Reinforce commercial value monitoring by supporting visibility on MVC/MRC governance, indexation, billing reconciliation, discount governance, scope creep, and operational leakage in collaboration with accountable functions. • Clarify role boundaries between Sales, Legal, Contract Management, Customer Success, Project Management, Finance, Delivery, and Operations, ensuring Contract Management acts as a governance and risk management function, not as a substitute for Legal advice or functional ownership.
**Sales enablement, training and knowledge sharing**
› Design and deliver recurring training for Sales, account, and regional teams on contract standards, risk identification, governance routines, escalation routes, and approved ways of working.
› Act as a practical advisor to Sales and business stakeholders on live deals, providing commercially aware guidance while ensuring appropriate Legal, Finance, and SME involvement.
› Build and maintain contract playbooks, clause guidance, standard positions, fallback libraries, deal-review checklists, and approval matrices.
› Coach stakeholders on post-signature obligations so that account and delivery teams understand what has been contractually committed.
› Facilitate monthly knowledge-sharing sessions and SME deep dives, including open Q&A forums, to build stakeholder confidence, strengthen contracting know-how, and promote consistent best practice across global sales teams.

• Minimum of 8 years’ experience in contract management, contract operations, commercial management, business excellence, transformation, or legal-commercial roles.
• Experience supporting high-value strategic projects, complex commercial agreements, and post-signature governance in an international environment.
• Strong understanding of contractual risk management, commercial governance, lifecycle processes, operating model deployment, and stakeholder accountability boundaries.
• Experience working across matrixed, multi-country organisations and influencing distributed stakeholder groups.

• Strong understanding of contractual risk management, commercial governance, lifecycle processes, operating model deployment, and stakeholder accountability boundaries.

**2) Network Security & Zero Trust**
* Apply **Zero Trust principles** across identity-aware segmentation, micro/macro segmentation (e.g., SDN, NSX‐T, ACI, TGW/Cloud WAN firewalls), secure east‐west and north‐south flows.
* Define **security guardrails** (FWaaS, NGFW, WAF, IDS/IPS, DDoS, DNS security), key management, and policy-as-code; integrate with SIEM/SOAR.

* Engineer for **high availability** (multi‐AZ/region, fast reroute, ECMP, anycast, graceful restart) and **deterministic performance** for latency‐sensitive workloads (including telco and real‐time apps).
* Define **traffic engineering** strategies (QoS/CoS, policy‐based routing, segment routing, MPLS/EVPN/VXLAN, SR‐MPLS/SRv6).
* Design **DR and failover** topologies; conduct chaos/resilience testing and capacity planning.
**4) Automation, IaC & Observability**
* Drive **automation‐first** delivery using **Terraform/Ansible/Python** and network controllers/SDKs; embed **policy‐as‐code** and compliance checks into CI/CD.
* Implement **observability**: streaming telemetry, NetFlow/IPFIX, SNMP, syslog, synthetic testing, path analytics, digital experience monitoring (DEM).

**5) Cloud & Edge Networking**
* Architect **cloud networking** at scale: VPC/VNet design, routing domains, NAT, ingress/egress, hybrid connectivity (DX/Interconnect/VPN), service discovery, PrivateLink/PSC.

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research.
We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.
Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.
**The role**
The Institute for Communication Systems (ICS) home of the 5G and 6G Innovation Centre (5GIC/6GIC) is looking to recruit **Research Fellow in Analog Computing for Advanced Communication Systems**. The successful candidate will be part of the Wireless Systems Lab group and will have the opportunity to work very close with our industrial partners as well as with academic partners all over the world.
The post holder will undertake research into ultra-low-power analog and mixed-signal computing architectures for future communication systems, with particular emphasis on receiver processing and architectures that reduce or remove reliance on conventional high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion.
The research will investigate how signal-processing operations traditionally implemented digitally can be reformulated and realised using analog, mixed-signal and in-memory computing technologies. Particular emphasis will be placed on the co-design of algorithms and hardware, circuit- and system-level modelling, and evaluation of the resulting architectures in terms of communication performance, power consumption, latency, precision and implementation complexity. The post holder will be expected to be able to set, define and work towards achieving targets, disseminate results and document work done.
**About you**
ICS is the largest academic research institute in Europe specialising in all aspects of ICT (Information and Communication Technologies). It is home to over 200 researchers with expertise in all communication and broadcasting systems and has developed the best in class large scale testbeds for research and innovation and enjoys the state-of-the-art lab and computing facilities.
Established in 2012, 5GIC is the world’s first dedicated centre in researching end-to-end aspects of 5G and works closely with national and international leading academic institutes and key industrial partners. In November 2020, 6GIC was officially launched with parallel research undertaken in both 5G+ and 6G for 2030+.
The post holder must have expertise in the following:
* Strong knowledge and research experience in analogue circuit design, particularly for low-power signal processing, computing or communication applications.
* Experience in circuit-level modelling and simulation, including the ability to evaluate power/energy consumption and relevant circuit non-idealities.
* Experience or strong knowledge of algorithm–hardware co-design, including the mapping of mathematical or signal-processing operations onto practical hardware subject to noise, precision, dynamic-range, variability and implementation constraints.
* Strong analytical, modelling and programming skills, including experience with MATLAB and/or Python, and the ability to communicate research findings effectively in written and oral form.
It would be desirable but not essential for the post holder to also have:
* Experience with in-memory computing architectures, including memristive/ReRAM or other emerging-device technologies.
* Knowledge of signal processing and communication systems, particularly channel estimation, detection, decoding, optimisation or linear algebra.
* A track record of high-quality peer-reviewed publications in analog/mixed-signal circuits, in-memory/neuromorphic computing, signal processing, communications or related areas.
For informal enquiries please contact: k.nikitopoulos@surrey.ac.uk

To apply, please submit your application with a CV and Cover Letter online via the University of Surrey jobs portal.

Oxford, England, United Kingdom
**About IonQ:**
IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance. Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.
**Location:**Oxford, England, UK **Working pattern:** Hybrid
**Role:**
We are looking for a Senior Silicon Validation Engineer to join our Cryo-CMOS IC team at IonQ Oxford. You will lead the validation and characterisation of analogue and mixed-signal ASICs for our trapped-ion quantum processors, from test planning and platform development through first-silicon bring-up, debug and system integration.
This is a hands-on technical role. You will shape our validation architecture, build reusable hardware and software, and provide the evidence needed to make confident silicon acceptance decisions. The work includes room-temperature silicon validation and silicon characterisation at cryogenic temperatures (around 4 kelvin), on packaged parts, chip-on-board assemblies and bare die on a cryogenic probe station.
**Responsibilities:**
You will own validation delivery across chip and system interfaces, working closely with analogue and digital design, verification, modelling, firmware and systems engineers. You will turn requirements into measurable tests, prepare platforms before silicon arrives and resolve failures across the chip, board and software.
As a Senior engineer, you will set technical standards, guide other engineers and improve coverage, repeatability and test efficiency across successive ASIC generations.
Key responsibilities include:
* Own the silicon validation strategy, plans, acceptance criteria and readiness reviews, with traceability from block and system requirements to tests, results and unresolved risks.
* Present the silicon acceptance report to the Cryo-CMOS IC Lead and programme stakeholders.
* Lead first-silicon bring-up and characterisation of sample-and-hold and switch arrays, DACs, ADCs, references, amplifiers, switches, regulators, clocking and device-level test structures, across supply, temperature, operating modes and device variation, with sound calibration and measurement uncertainty.
* Develop validation boards, fixtures and reusable Python automation, instrument drivers and regression suites, addressing signal integrity, grounding, power integrity and measurement access, with version-controlled tests and reproducible data analysis.
* Plan and lead cryogenic measurements with specialist colleagues, including bare-die probing and the cold signal chain, and drive failures to root cause, separating silicon defects from board, firmware and test artefacts and correlating results with simulations, device models and foundry or partner data.
* Influence testability before tape-out, coordinate validation with external design partners, the foundry and other IonQ sites.
* Lead technical reviews, mentor engineers and document methods to improve throughput, data quality and reuse.
**Requirements:**
You will bring substantial experience in analogue or mixed-signal silicon validation and characterisation, with ownership of multiple silicon bring-up programmes. A degree in electrical or electronic engineering, or equivalent practical experience, is expected. You should combine hands-on laboratory skills with sound judgement on test coverage, measurement confidence and programme risk.
You’d be a great fit with:
* Strong electronics fundamentals and experience validating precision signal chains, data converters or power-management circuits, including their digital control interfaces.
* Practical expertise with oscilloscopes, precision sources and meters, signal generators, spectrum and logic analysers; confidence designing reliable low-noise, low-leakage measurements.
* Strong Python programming for instrument control, automated testing and statistical analysis; disciplined use of Git or equivalent version control and maintainable test software.
* Experience designing and debugging test PCBs, reviewing layouts and working with interfaces such as SPI, I2C, JTAG and custom shift-register chains, alongside embedded firmware or FPGA-based platforms.
* A record of resolving complex chip, board and software interactions through structured experiments and collaboration.
* Experience leading technical projects, mentoring engineers and communicating evidence, uncertainty and decisions in clear written reports.
Useful additional experience includes cryogenic or other extreme-temperature testing; wafer or bare-die probing; early-stage IP or test-chip evaluation; FPGA development and C/C++; circuit simulation; and production test correlation. Prior quantum computing is welcome but not required.
**Benefits:**
Be part of a team that’s shaping the future of quantum. We offer more than just a role, you’ll join a world class community of scientists, engineers and innovators working to unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
We offer a range of benefits, including opportunities to further your career alongside industry leaders, a competitive salary with IonQ stock options, an annual performance bonus, generous annual leave, flexible hybrid working, private medical and dental insurance for you and your family, and much more.
Join us and be part of the future of quantum computing.

**YEAR-IN INDUSTRY ENGINEERING PLACEMENT**
**Ready to put your engineering studies into practice?**
Join our growing Engineering team in **Hucknall, UK**, for a **12-month Year in Industry placement** and gain hands-on experience working on aerospace projects.
Opportunities are available across:
* **Manufacturing Engineering**
* **Manufacturing Engineering – Special Processes**
* **Design Engineering**
* **Combustion R&T Design Engineering**
These placements will help you develop your skills, learn from experienced colleagues and gain valuable insight into engineering within the aerospace industry, but it isn’t just about what you’ll learn from us, we want to learn from you too**.** You’ll bring fresh ideas and perspectives, contribute to real engineering challenges and become a valued part of the team throughout your placement.
We will ask you to indicate your preferred engineering area when you apply but we will consider your preference alongside your skills, experience and our business requirements when making final placement decisions.
**Explore the roles below to find out where your Year in Industry could take you.**
**Manufacturing Engineering – Key Responsibilities**
* Develop and maintain Methods of Manufacture and technical packages for shop floor use, including instructions, stage drawings, and routers.
* Apply Build in Quality tools (e.g. Process Maps, PFMEAs, Control Plans) and use data analysis software to monitor and improve process capability.
* Plan and manage engineering projects aligned with UK-Spec competencies, resolving technical issues and collaborating across design, quality, manufacturing, and purchasing teams.
* Support production flow and drive continuous improvement to reduce concessions, rework, and costs.
* Contribute to the development of new manufacturing processes using emerging technologies.
**Manufacturing Engineering – Special Processes Key Responsibilities**
* Control and develop the special processes required to support manufacture of components within ITP Aero UK
* Ensure that engineering specifications are satisfied for new part introduction and ongoing manufacture.
* Provide technical support on all material and special processes, ensuring the site is NADCAP compliant, accredited in the required timescales and maintains any existing approvals.
* Ensure process compliance to National and International Standards through both the generation of shop floor instructions and the participation in audit procedures
* Help deliver process data cards and procedures, process or stage drawings and Methods of Manufacture both for domestically manufactured parts and for parts manufactured in the external supply network.
* Help maintain operator training and qualification requirements for special processes.
* Support the selection, justification, acquisition and commissioning of new processing equipment.
**Design Engineering – Key Responsibilities**
* Design jet engine components that meet functional, physical, and manufacturing requirements, following the full lifecycle from concept to in-service support.
* Deliver high-quality components on time, working within Integrated Project Teams and in line with ITP Aero UK policies.
* Understand customer needs and develop robust, cost-effective design solutions that consider safety, maintainability, and repair.
* Support the Zero Defects journey by integrating manufacturing and measurement capabilities into design, applying lean principles and improving design tools and methods.
* Create compliant technical documentation, compile Bills of Materials (BOMs), and support configuration processes.
* Use CAD software (ideally Siemens NX and Team centre); training will be provided.
**Combustion R&T Engineering – Key Responsibilities**
* Support the development of ITP Aero’s growing Combustor Design and Technology capability.
* Contribute to the design and manufacture of aerospace combustion systems for conventional fuels, SAF and future hydrogen technologies.
* Work with colleagues across the UK and Spain to develop innovative combustion technologies within a Research & Technology (R&T) environment.
* Use CAD Design and gain exposure to Additive Manufacturing.
* Get involved in practical, hands-on engineering activities, including testing.
* Work with different engineering teams, including Manufacturing, Stress and Aerothermal.
* Bring curiosity, adaptability and a willingness to learn in a fast-moving R&T environment.
*The aviation industry is living a new dawn as it moves towards a greener future and zero carbon propulsion: being part of it by designing the jet engines of the future is very exciting!*
**Uplift**: A key requirement of the placement programme is to be a STEM Ambassador and support Uplift, our STEM outreach initiative. You will have the opportunity to inspire future talent, build your communication and leadership skills, and get involved in activities such as coding camps, STEM workshops, and school and community events.
**What profile are we looking for?**
**Essential criteria**
* Working towards a minimum of a HNC in Aerospace / General / Materials / Mechanical / Manufacturing Engineering.
* Has good communications skills and the ability to influence at all levels of the organisation.
**Desirable criteria**
* A background in aerospace engineering is not essential.
* Sound understanding of problem-solving techniques such as DMAIC principles.
* An ability to apply logical, analytical and **innovative** thinking on a range of technical problems and make balanced decisions across technical and business parameters is a prerequisite
* Strong technical knowledge in mechanical design methodologies and, ideally, understands cross discipline engineering concepts which may include but are not limited to thermal and mechanical analysis, manufacturing engineering, aerodynamics, thermodynamics, cost engineering and product definition.
* Ability to effectively plan engineering tasks that are part of complex projects involving several departments.
**Who will I work with (in my team and in collaboration with other areas)?**
You will work at ITP Aero from its site in Hucknall, Nottinghamshire under the guidance of professionals with extensive experience in the sector in a leading company in aeronautical engines and components that ranks among the top companies in the global aeronautical industry.

## About Kernel
Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?
Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.
Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.
Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at **Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion** already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

## About this role
Salary: Range - 50,480 - 63,100 Closing date: 27th October Contract type: Permanent, Full Time Interview dates: Week commencing 9th November The Wellcome Trust is a global charitable foundation. We improve health for everyone by funding science, leading policy and advocacy campaigns, and building partnerships.
We plan to spend £16bn over the next ten years, funding new discoveries in life, health, and wellbeing, and taking on three global health challenges: mental health, infectious disease and climate and health. These challenges need the bold science we support, but they won't be solved by science alone. Where in Wellcome will I be working?
You will be working within the Communications team in Corporate Affairs, reporting to the Content Lead. The Communications team helps Wellcome connect audiences with the ideas, evidence, people and partnerships that drive progress in health research.
Through compelling storytelling and audience-focused communications, the team develops content and campaigns that support Wellcome's strategic priorities, builds engagement with key audiences, and strengthens Wellcome's influence across science, health and research.
Working closely with colleagues across Wellcome, the team creates content that helps audiences understand complex issues and discoveries, translating them into clear, accessible and engaging communications across digital channels. What will I be doing?
As a Senior Content & Social Media Producer, you will lead the planning, creation, commissioning and optimisation of digital content that supports Wellcome's strategic priorities across health, science and research.
You'll develop audience-focused content and campaigns across a range of digital channels, ensuring content is engaging, accessible and tailored to different audiences.
You will play a key role in strengthening Wellcome's digital communications capability, championing best practice in content production, visual storytelling, social media, accessibility and audience engagement. Working collaboratively across Wellcome, you will help ensure content reaches the right audiences and delivers measurable impact.
As a Senior Content & Social Media Producer, you will: Lead the planning, creation and commissioning of digital content and campaigns that support Wellcome's strategic priorities. Translate complex scientific, research and policy topics into accessible, engaging and audience-centred storytelling.
Produce and commission creative assets including video, photography, animation and infographics, working with internal teams and external suppliers. Develop content distribution and audience engagement strategies, working across paid, owned and partner channels to maximise reach and impact.
Use audience insights, analytics and performance data to optimise content and inform future communications activity. Champion best practice in digital content, social media and storytelling, sharing expertise and developing capability across the organisation.
Build and manage relationships with agencies, freelancers, creators and external partners to deliver high-quality content. Contribute to a diverse and inclusive culture across the organisation, collaborating across departments. Is this job for me?
We're looking for two experienced digital content professional with a strong track record of creating engaging content and delivering successful multi-channel digital campaigns. You'll be an excellent storyteller and editor, capable of turning complex ideas into compelling content for a range of audiences and platforms.
You will be comfortable managing multiple projects simultaneously, working at pace and collaborating with a broad range of stakeholders. You'll combine creativity with strong editorial judgement and a data-informed approach, using audience insight and performance metrics to continuously improve content effectiveness.
This role would suit someone who enjoys working in a collaborative environment, is passionate about digital communications and is excited by the opportunity to help communicate important developments in health, science and research to audiences around the world.
We are looking to hire two people, with a specialist focus across: Climate and Health Discovery To apply for this role please submit an up to date CV and answer 2 application questions including the area you are interested in, demonstrating that you meet the minimum requirements for the role.
Minimum Criteria Significant experience in digital content planning, production and publishing within a complex organisation. Experience commissioning and managing external agencies, creators or production partners. Significant experience creating compelling digital and social media content, with strong editorial judgement and storytelling skills.
Experience planning and delivering multi-channel digital campaigns, including content distribution and audience engagement strategies. Experience using content management systems and social media platforms alongside analytics and performance data to inform content decisions and evaluate success.
