# Senior Designer - Special Projects
£55k-£65k
### The Role
This is not a traditional design role. We’re looking for a Special Projects Designer.
Special projects are the things we make when Koto is the client. Ideas, thought leadership and events that take our brand somewhere new, and give us a chance to make things we wouldn’t normally get to make. Things like OFF, our growing mix of editorial content and live events. Seasoned, our platform supporting design education, and CcType, our very own type foundry. These are just the beginning, which is exactly where you come in.
You’ll help us define the ideas, the design and art direction that bring these happenings, digitally and physically to life. As we evolve, these things are becoming bigger and more varied. Events, ventures and content with unexpected collaborations.
This is a unique role for someone entrepreneurial, someone who can spot a good idea, push it further, then further again, then turn it into something people notice, share and talk about. Motion skills are nice to have, but not essential.
You will work closely with Jowey Roden, Koto’s Chief Creative Officer; Dan Witchell, Executive Creative Director in London; and our Global Marketing team, while collaborating with creatives across our global studios. Motion skills are welcome but not essential. What matters most is strong ideas, excellent taste, curiosity and the ability to learn quickly.
Here’s a preview of your playground.
### Your Responsibilities
1. You partner closely with Koto’s Chief Creative Officer, London’s Executive Creative Director and Global Marketing team to shape how Koto shows up in the world.
2. You bring a clear creative vision to Koto’s brand, developing strong concepts, visual systems and work that strengthens our reputation and supports our ambitions.
3. You co-lead design across special projects such as Seasoned, CcType and the OFF ecosystem, while helping us imagine and launch new ventures, events, collaborations and products.
4. In a team setting, you take projects from first thought to final delivery, moving confidently between concept development, design, art direction and production.
5. You lead the visual output of Koto’s social channels, creating branded content that earns attention, engages the right audiences and works naturally across platforms.
6. You design across a broad range of formats, including brand identity, campaigns, editorial, events, presentations, digital experiences, merchandise and moving image.
7. You bring fresh thinking to studio launches, cultural moments, hiring campaigns and celebrations, turning them into creative opportunities rather than traditional announcements.
8. You experiment with new tools, formats and production techniques. Motion experience is a plus, but curiosity, initiative and the ability to learn quickly matter more.
9. You work closely with designers, strategists, writers, filmmakers, developers, photographers and external makers, bringing in the right skills to make each idea stronger.
10. You take clear ownership of your work, managing projects with pace and care. You present ideas confidently, respond well to feedback and play an active role in our London studio and wider global team.
### Our Responsibilities
1. We will give you meaningful access to your manager and Koto’s creative leadership, supporting your development while giving you room to shape the role and propose new ideas.
2. We will actively reward performance through promotions, pay increases and a discretionary annual bonus of up to 10% of salary.
3. We will ensure Koto is an equal and inclusive environment for every employee.
4. We will support family leave and offer significant paid maternity and paternity policies.
5. We will encourage you to take 25 days of annual leave, alongside UK bank holidays, one additional day for each year of service capped at five days, and our studio closure between Christmas and New Year.
6. We will contribute an additional 3% for anyone joining the Scottish Widows pension scheme.
7. We provide a monthly employee wellness allowance of £75 through Juno.
8. We offer access to YCN and fund relevant training opportunities for employees looking to develop their skills and careers.
9. We reward five years of service with £5,000 and five additional days of holiday. We reward ten years with £10,000 and four weeks of additional holiday.
10. We will give you opportunities to work from and travel to Koto studios globally, with appropriate planning around projects and studio needs.
### Our Culture
* At Koto we encourage our team to be 'rationally optimistic\*\*’\*\* about the potential of our work, our clients, their businesses, and the power of brand.
* We pursue the best briefs, want to inspire meaningful work, and for those interested provide an opportunity to make the work of their lives. We are actively cultivating leadership, culture and spaces to encourage this.
* We work in person with an optional WFH day on Friday, and an additional twenty days remote a year. We believe this produces the best work, mentoring opportunities, collective learning and culture.
* We encourage autonomy in each member of our team, allowing them to manage their own time, hours and personal commitments appropriately to complete work.

# Principal, Data & AI Integration
* London, United Kingdom
Mintel is the world’s leading market intelligence agency. Increasingly, our clients don’t come to Mintel; Mintel goes to them. They use our research and data inside their own systems — through AI assistants and agents, APIs, data feeds, dashboards and internal research tools — and combine it with their own business data and third-party data. Clients who work this way stay with us longer and get more from us, and the integrations that make it possible are already live. This is the next frontier for Mintel, and we are hiring someone to make it excellent. You will understand how clients integrate Mintel into their own ecosystems and make sure what we deliver doesn’t just work, but fits the way they actually work: from the question a client asks in their own tool, through what Mintel returns, to what they do with the answer next. This is not a traditional product or UX role. Mintel does not own the end user experience in an integration; our clients do. What we own is what we send: how our content, data and capabilities are structured, described and delivered so they are usable, trustworthy and recognisably Mintel in environments we don’t control. A large part of your time will be spent with clients: understanding their workflows and what they are trying to achieve, seeing how Mintel actually shows up in their work, and removing the obstacles that stand between them and the value. The rest is turning what you learn into what we return. Our engineers own the integration’s code; you own what it should return. You will work hand in hand with our Senior Director, Data Product. Together you decide what is on offer: she owns whether the data is ready and reliable; you own how it works from the client’s side and whether it achieves their goal. Neither ships without the other. You will also work daily with our engineers, architects and product managers. This is a senior individual-contributor role. It carries no team. It is principal-level because the work has to move engineers, product managers and the data team without authority over any of them. **What you’ll do** **Understand clients and what they are really trying to achieve** * Take a consultative approach: run client discovery, observe workflows, and dig past the requested feature to the outcome behind it. Most clients want to innovate faster; the interesting part is how differently each one goes about it.
* Understand how clients combine Mintel with their own and third-party data, and where their systems and processes get in the way.
* Decide what we standardise and what we tailor: find the patterns that work for many clients and recognise when an individual client genuinely needs something different.
* Build a library of real use cases, case studies and representative client scenarios that shapes product decisions and equips our commercial teams.
**Shape the integration experience**
* Own the integration-facing contract, in partnership with Data Product: what we expose, what it is called, how it is described and what each element carries, so that whatever a client’s system composes is clear, traceable and valuable.
* Set the standard for a good integration experience and review new Mintel capabilities against it, so integration is part of discovery rather than an afterthought.
* Collaborate closely with Data Product and Engineering to turn client evidence into the roadmap and into real improvements, not just recommendations.
**Evaluate and improve**
* Test how Mintel capabilities actually appear and perform in representative client environments, before and after every change.
* Watch what assistants and systems actually call, where they fail and where they fall silent, and keep a set of real client questions to run against every change. An assistant that stops finding Mintel useful never tells you.
* When something comes out wrong, work out whether the cause is the integration-facing definition, the returned output, the data or the client’s implementation, and bring in the right owner.
**Develop best practice and enablement**
* Give clients practical guidance and examples when they are still shaping their integration approach, without designing or building their specific system.
* Help Sales and Account Management understand the shift from websites to integrations: what is possible, what is not, and which delivery route fits which need.
* Contribute to Mintel’s thought leadership on integration experiences.
**What we’re looking for**
This role combines client discovery, product thinking, information design and technical fluency. We are specifically looking for a mix of experience across technical solution consulting, API-first or integration products, and AI-assisted or data-rich products, in whatever combination you have built it. Few people have all of it from one job; most of the people we want have crossed at least one boundary. **You will need:**
* **A consultative mindset and an appetite for clients.** Expect around 30% of your time talking to clients and, where it helps, travelling to see their workflows first-hand. You are genuinely interested in unblocking individual clients, and you turn each one into something that works for many. You have to want this, not tolerate it.
* **Technical fluency**. You can read an integration and the data it returns, and test it the way a client’s system would. You understand APIs, MCP, AI assistants, authentication and data exchange, and you pick up new tools quickly as the landscape changes. You are not here to build the integration; our engineers do that, and they will treat you as a peer because you understand their work.
* **Information design**. You can look at the raw data behind an answer and say whether a client reading it would trust it, and restructure it so they would. This is design applied to data, not to screens.
* **Product judgement.** You balance client needs, business goals, data constraints and technical reality, and explain the trade-offs clearly.
* **Influence without authority.** You create alignment across Product, Data Product, Engineering, Architecture and Commercial teams, and you communicate well with technical and non-technical audiences, including clients.
**It helps if you have:**
* Worked on API, platform, data-sharing or integration products, or on products consumed inside customer-controlled tools.
* Experience with AI-assisted workflows, enterprise search or knowledge platforms.
* Developed standards, case studies or practices that other teams adopted.
**Before you apply, four things to know:**
* This is an individual-contributor role. There is no team to manage, now or planned.
* There are no screens. The design work is in what our integrations return: the data, its structure and how it is described.
* You decide what the integrations should return; our engineers build them. If you would rather be building, this isn’t the role.
* The role will change shape as the technology and our clients do. You will be defining it as you go, not inheriting a settled job.
**What you'll get in return:**
* A culture that supports true collaboration whilst embracing remote working with a company wide hybrid working week.
* Approach to personal development where we encourage individuals to grow and share what they’ve learned.
* Social events, both within the department and across the company
* Generous holiday allowance with the opportunity to buy back additional holiday.

Working independently as a technical specialist and collaborating across manufacturing, engineering, quality, validation, and digital teams, you will help translate advanced automation technology into safe, efficient, validated manufacturing operations, with opportunities to explore emerging digital and Generative AI-enabled solutions.

Troubleshoot and optimise PLCs, Emerson DeltaV distributed control systems, HMIs, instrumentation, industrial networks, machine controls, servo and motion systems, vision technologies, and equipment interfaces to maintain reliable manufacturing operations.
* Become a technical expert in automated packaging technologies: Support the introduction, operation, and continuous improvement of automated labelling and secondary packaging equipment, including labelers, cartoners, case packers, serialization and aggregation systems, vision inspection equipment, printers, scanners, conveyors, robotics, and material-handling systems. Identify opportunities to simplify operations, reduce changeover times, and improve packaging-line consistency, flexibility, and throughput.
* Deliver automation projects from design through manufacturing start-up: Support new and modified automation systems throughout their complete engineering lifecycle, including design, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, qualification, validation, start-up, and handover to routine manufacturing. Contribute to new-equipment introduction, technology transfer, scale-up, and commercial manufacturing readiness.
* Strengthen process automation and control systems: Provide technical support for existing drug substance manufacturing automation, with particular emphasis on Emerson DeltaV and Allen-Bradley/Rockwell PLC-based systems. Diagnose complex control-system issues spanning instrumentation, electrical systems, industrial communications, automation logic, and mechanical equipment interfaces.
* Develop robust automation engineering documentation: Create, review, and maintain automation lifecycle documentation, including User Requirement Specification (URS) inputs, functional and design specifications, control strategies, configuration records, engineering drawings, risk assessments, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), troubleshooting guides, and engineering standards. Ensure documentation supports effective system operation, maintainability, and regulatory compliance.
* Collaborate with equipment manufacturers and system integrators: Work directly with Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), automation suppliers, and system integrators to support equipment design, technical troubleshooting, upgrades, modifications, and performance improvements. Help ensure vendor-delivered solutions meet Moderna's operational, technical, safety, and quality expectations.
* Lead technical investigations and sustainable problem resolution: Independently investigate automation failures, recurring equipment downtime, quality events, and manufacturing process deviations. Apply structured root cause analysis to complex multidisciplinary problems, developing and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) that address underlying causes and prevent recurrence.
* Use manufacturing data to improve equipment performance: Analyse equipment and process data to identify recurring failures, performance trends, and opportunities to improve equipment reliability, throughput, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), changeover performance, and operational robustness. Leverage manufacturing historians, MES, CMMS, and available analytics capabilities to support evidence-based engineering decisions.
* Maintain validated and compliant automation systems: Support GxP activities, including formal change controls, deviations, CAPAs, risk assessments, qualification, and validation. Partner closely with Quality and Validation to ensure packaging and process automation systems remain in a controlled and validated state throughout their operational lifecycle, with appropriate consideration of electronic records, data integrity, and computerized system requirements.
* Optimise equipment and systems integration: Troubleshoot interactions between packaging equipment, automation platforms, industrial networks, and plant-level digital systems. Contribute to robust communication and data exchange across operational technology (OT) and information technology (IT) environments, supporting equipment connectivity, serialization, and manufacturing-system integration.
* Drive reliability and lifecycle improvements: Contribute to equipment lifecycle management, preventive maintenance strategies, spare-parts planning, and technology obsolescence management. Apply reliability engineering principles to improve equipment availability, reduce unplanned downtime, and strengthen long-term manufacturing performance.
* Explore digital innovation and emerging technologies: Identify opportunities to leverage digital manufacturing tools, advanced analytics, and approved Generative AI-enabled solutions to support troubleshooting, technical knowledge management, engineering documentation, and equipment performance optimisation while maintaining appropriate GxP and data integrity controls.
* Collaborate across a multidisciplinary manufacturing environment: Work closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Maintenance, Quality, Validation, Supply Chain, Automation, Digital, and external technical partners to deliver integrated packaging and process automation solutions that meet operational requirements, business objectives, and patient needs. Communicate complex technical findings clearly to manufacturing colleagues, technical stakeholders, leadership, and equipment vendors.
* Provide flexible manufacturing support: Take ownership of technical issues through resolution in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, balancing competing priorities and working independently. Provide occasional off-hours, weekend, and holiday support as manufacturing operations require.

* Bachelor of Science degree in **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline.

## **About Niantic Spatial**
AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.
That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.
In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.
Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.
## **About the Role**
You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.
The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.
You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model.
**What You'll Do**
* **Geospatial Registration** — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data.
* **3D Geometry & Correspondence** — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP.
* **Data & Evaluation** — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production.
* **Learning-Based 3D Reasoning** — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling.
* **Production Robustness** — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration** — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems.
* **Research Communication** — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate.
## **What You'll Bring**
* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience.
* Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area.
* Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion.
* The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously.
* Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy).
* Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems.
* A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data.
* Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines.
## **Nice to Have**
* PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued.
* A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS.
* Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors.
* Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data.
* Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery.

## About Nous
**Nous is an AI agent** that takes some of the load of life; making good decisions and acting for our users in areas where they’re not the experts or aren’t paying enough attention. We've started with optimising bills, where we're already saving households thousands, and are now expanding into new categories. Similar to how Amazon picked books as its first category and grew from there.
**We’re growing fast, and it's working.** 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.
We've just launched two more novel new products (on top of our existing bill optimisation). Insurance: we're the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use Open Banking to draw pretty graphs – we're the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.
It would be easy to look at this and think we've got it all figured out. But we've only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher.
**We’re building a new category of product** which is hard, so we’ve stacked the deck in our favour: an experienced founding team with multiple exits, and investors including the founders of Monzo, Wise, Booking.com, lastminute.com, Onfido, Funding Circle, Tide, Habito and more.
Still - **the problems we’re solving are hard**. *‘Talk is cheap’* applies to agents too. To have REAL impact, agents need to break out of the sandbox and take action in the real world where there are consequences. This means solving all the hard, thorny, interesting, frustrating problems the real world has to offer.
## ## **The role**
What Nous does for members can feel simple: helping them understand their bills, save money, and avoid admin. Delivering that reliably at scale is much harder.
You’ll join the Operations team at the heart of the business, working on the difficult real-world problems that sit between our members, our product, external suppliers and the systems that make Nous work.
This is not a traditional customer operations role. You’ll spend time close to our members, understanding their questions, investigating things that have gone wrong and learning in detail how our service works. We think that matters: the best systems are usually built by people who have seen the underlying problems first-hand.
But we don’t want you simply to get faster at doing manual work. We want you to spot the pattern, understand why the problem exists, and help build a better way of doing it.
That might mean redesigning a process, building an automation, using AI to remove repetitive work, querying data to understand what is happening, improving an internal tool, or working with Product and Engineering on a more fundamental fix.
You don't need to arrive knowing all of the tools we use. We care much more about how quickly you learn them.
We’re looking for someone early in their career who is unusually curious, quick to learn and good at figuring things out. You might already have built automations or small products yourself. You might instead have worked in operations, consulting, product, analytics or another demanding environment and found yourself constantly looking for better ways to do things.
Either way, we want someone who gets excited by a problem they don't immediately know how to solve.
You’ll have a lot of support from experienced operators, engineers and product people, but also be given a lot of responsibility unusually early in your career. The aim is for you to quickly become someone who can take an undefined operational problem, understand it properly and build a robust solution.
It’s a rare chance to learn how a fast-growing technology company actually works from the inside while building the systems that allow it to scale.

You’re smart, curious, ambitious and unusually high-agency.
You don't need a long list of technical tools on your CV. We care much more about how you think, how quickly you learn and what you do when you encounter something you don't understand.

* Learn unusually quickly and enjoy tackling problems you haven't seen before
* Are technically curious and actively experiment with AI and new tools to make yourself more effective
* Have evidence that you like building things, whether that's automations, side projects, spreadsheets, scripts, internal tools, processes or something completely different
* Are comfortable getting into the detail and tracing a problem until you understand what is really happening
* Can take something messy and ambiguous and impose structure on it
* Are naturally empathetic and enjoy understanding what a customer actually needs
* Communicate clearly and directly
* Are comfortable working directly with customers and frontline problems, and see that as a source of insight
* Take ownership rather than waiting to be told exactly what to do
This role is ideal for someone early in their career who wants a steep learning curve, real responsibility and the chance to work as part of a team solving difficult problems.

Clinic workflows sit close to clinical decisions even when the work itself is administrative. A patient can reply to a booking message with a symptom, a routine result can need urgent review, and a harmless-looking exception can change the risk entirely.

Every day, support teams spend thousands of hours on the same questions. Where is my order? How do I return this? Which product should I choose? Can I change my delivery address?
Octocom builds AI agents for support and sales for consumer businesses. Our agents handle conversations independently across chat, email, and phone, from order tracking and returns to product guidance and order changes. Businesses get faster responses, lower support costs, and more sales.

Octocom can already do far more than the outside world understands. The website is where that gap closes. You will be our first dedicated web designer: the person who sets the visual standard for the company and personally ships it.
The core of the job is the website. You'll expand and improve octocom.ai with pages that explain the product clearly and make a visitor think: these people are building something world-class. Social content, decks, and ads are not the focus.
The founders give you the substance: what the product does, why it matters, and rough ideas for what a page should say. You decide how it reads and how it looks. Copy and layout are one craft, and you own both.

Octopus Money is hiring a DevOps Engineer to own and evolve the AWS platform that our customer-facing products run on. ## About otum
otum is the data and automation engineering team for companies without one. We build the data platforms, back-office automation, and software companies usually need an in-house team for. Senior engineers scope each system, build it, and stay accountable for it.

We are a senior team, working across the UK and internationally. Teams stay small, everyone works directly with the client, and every build is reviewed by a senior engineer before it reaches them.

## Role
You build AI workflows into a client's own stack that do the manual document and data work, reliably enough to trust with real decisions. You make the model's output verifiable, route the uncertain cases to a human, and hand over code the client owns. This is the AI side of otum.

You join the AI side of otum, working on our AI Workflows builds. Teams are small and you work directly with the client's operations and domain people. A senior engineer reviews every build before it reaches the client, and you review others' work in turn.

Build AI workflows that read the documents and data a client runs on, extract the fields into a schema, and drive the next action, matching, updating records, routing, and flagging risks.
Layer deterministic checks over the model's output, business rules and validation a client can inspect, so a guess that breaks the rules is caught by code rather than posted.
Route low-confidence cases to a human with a per-field confidence score, and turn their fixes into new test cases.
Practise eval-driven development, measuring field-level accuracy on a golden set of the client's real documents before anything goes live.
Build it to run inside the client's own cloud, so their documents never leave and nothing you process trains anyone's models, with an audit trail on every run.
Sit with the client to scope the first workflow and agree what good enough to trust actually means.
## What we're looking for
Several years building applied AI or ML systems in production, not just demos, with LLMs or document-processing pipelines.
Experience with structured extraction, evaluation (golden sets, field-level precision and recall), and confidence-based routing.
Comfortable layering deterministic validation over probabilistic output, and building human-in-the-loop review into a workflow.
Familiar with running models in a client's own cloud, model-agnostic, and integrating through existing APIs.
Able to work directly with a client, and to be honest about where AI is and is not reliable.
## Location
Remote. You can be based anywhere in the UK or internationally, as long as you keep a few hours of daily overlap with the team and the client. Some client calls are fixed, and there is the occasional trip to a client site.

The Savings & Retirement Deal Pricing team are responsible for producing the fees & premiums to send to clients in our global markets. * Following the investment markets and being able to translate and explain changes in the market conditions into changes to pricing. Work with the asset management team to agree investment assumptions for pricing.

* Ability to work independently on reviewing critically numbers coming out of the model, understanding what drives changes, sense-checking results (at the level appropriate for an analyst).

* Experience of transactions and/or pricing work is beneficial but not essential.
* Strong experience of Excel and actuarial modelling software (Tyche or similar)
* Good general understanding of market risks (interest rates, FX, credit spread, liquidity) and how they impact insurance capitalization.
* Strong communication skills. Able to communicate complex actuarial concepts to a range of audiences both verbally and written.

* Understanding of Pension Risk Transfer markets
* Understanding of life insurance company balance sheets and capital and profit reporting regimes (IFRS, Solvency II, US GAAP, BMA).

PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.
***This is a global remote opportunity. Please submit a cover letter along with your resume outlining your interest in the role and how your experience and qualifications align with the requirements of the position***
PATH’s AI Initiative is pioneering the use of generative AI and other advanced digital technologies to accelerate biomedical discovery, strengthen regulatory systems, and enhance the safety and scalability of digital healthcare.
**About the role:**
PATH leads a three-year programme, funded by the Gates Foundation, to test whether an AI co-scientist can help identify potential correlates of protection for vaccine development and shorten the path to licensing new and improved vaccines. The programme began with rotavirus and maternal RSV vaccination and will move to other diseases in its final phase.
In phase one, PATH used off-the-shelf co-scientist tools built by frontier AI labs to generate and rank candidate biomarkers for rotavirus and maternal RSV vaccination, with PATH scientists and external experts reviewing each cycle. Those reviews showed that the tools’ main limitations were shaped by the scientific knowledge they could access and how they weighed evidence on immunology, assays and trials. Phase two will focus on designing a small, open knowledge asset that measurably improves how an agentic tool generates and ranks vaccine science hypotheses.
Working under the supervision of the Deputy Director (AI4Science), the consultant will lead the expert process that produces this design. You'll help convene a technical advisory group of academic experts in evidence synthesis, biomedical data structuring and informatics. You'll work alongside PATH's own AI specialists and bring the group together with vaccine scientists who work on correlates. You'll draft the material the experts respond to, run the conversations, and take part in them as one of the technical voices. By the end of 2026 you'll turn their views into options for a decision with the Gates Foundation on which parts of the asset to build first.
The role suits a biomedical informatics or computational biology researcher who has built structured knowledge resources and has worked closely with domain scientists, ideally in infectious disease or vaccine research. If you are interested in helping shape a cutting-edge problem alongside leading experts in AI and biomedical science, with results that can have a positive impact on global health, this is the role for you.
**What you'll be doing:**
* Work with the PATH team to critically review the phase-one record and translate observed failure modes into an initial view of what the knowledge asset must contain.
* Draft a conceptual outline for a minimum viable knowledge asset.
* Brief and engage technical advisers and disease experts, individually and as a group, preparing the background material needed for each conversation.
* Design and co-facilitate an expert workshop, either as a single convening or a series of sessions, to agree methods for automated extraction from biomedical sources and approaches for scoring and prioritising knowledge, building on an evidence-quality scoring framework PATH has developed in related work.
* Reconcile and summarise expert opinion, noting where consensus was reached, where views differed, and the evidence or reasoning behind each position.
* Draft an options paper that sets out what to build first, the expected impact, cost and complexity, and how each element would be evaluated, with enough detail to scope the build that follows.
* Contribute to publications and presentations arising from the work, where the results warrant it.
**By December 2026 you'll have produced:**
* Briefing material for the advisers and experts
* A conceptual outline of the minimum viable knowledge asset
* A workshop design and a written synthesis of its conclusions
* An options paper to support the funding decision, which will form the basis of the programme's knowledge asset roadmap.
**Required skills and experience**:
* PhD, or equivalent research experience, in biomedical informatics, computational biology, bioinformatics or a related field.
* Hands-on experience designing or building structured biomedical knowledge resources, such as knowledge graphs, ontology-aligned databases, curated evidence tables or retrieval-augmented generation systems for scientific literature.
* Working familiarity with large language models and agentic systems, including how retrieval and tool access, for example through the Model Context Protocol, shape what a model produces.
* Experience running expert consultations, technical working groups or similar processes, and a record of synthesising their conclusions.
* Ideally, grounding in vaccine immunology or infectious disease sufficient to follow and contribute to technical discussions.
*We know great candidates won't always meet every listed qualification.*
*Research shows that some groups, on average, are more likely to self-select out if they feel they don't meet all requirements. If you're excited about the role and think you'd be a good fit, we encourage you to apply*.

#### **About Phorest**
Phorest started in 2002 on a busy salon reception desk as a simple text-reminder tool.
Today Phorest builds software and AI-powered tools used by more than 155,000 hair, beauty and medspa professionals worldwide. We’re a product-led SaaS company solving real-world problems across bookings, payments, marketing and business management, with a big focus on building great experiences for both the businesses we serve and the people who use our products. Everything we build helps the salon and medspa industry thrive.
We're also a Certified B Corp, and 25% of the company is owned by Phoresters. When the company grows, everyone has a stake in that.
#### **More about the team**
Our ambition is to become the number one platform for premium hair, beauty and aesthetics businesses globally. For our Product & Engineering teams, that means understanding the people behind those businesses and building thoughtful, reliable products that make a real difference to how they work. We start with understanding what matters to the people using our products, and work together to solve problems that make a real difference to their businesses. You’ll thrive here if you enjoy operating in an environment that moves with pace, who brings energy and creates clarity and momentum as we scale.
#### **The Opportunity**
As we grow, the systems and infrastructure that power our business must scale with it. We’re looking for a Director of Engineering to lead Payments and Foundations: payments engineering, infrastructure, security, business systems, and internal AI enablement.
Your teams will be responsible for enabling scale, growing revenue, and protecting the business we have built. Payments is a significant contributor to revenue and a major part of our growth plans. Its quality and reliability matter to both our customers’ businesses and our own.
This role is also central to our internal scaling strategy: making it easier for our teams to deliver excellent service as Phorest grows. Connected systems, better workflows, and practical use of AI should help us onboard customers faster, resolve issues more effectively, and serve more customers without a proportional increase in operational effort.
Alongside leading your domain, you will partner with the CTO and fellow Director of Engineering in running the engineering organisation. Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.
## **About the role**
We're looking for a Brand Marketing Lead to join our Brand & Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help own our brand marketing strategy and campaign execution across six European markets and be part of our marketing team as we scale our spend management platform. If you're excited about building category-defining campaigns that move Pleo from a good solution to the undisputed choice for mid-market finance leaders and are passionate about brand strategy and creative execution, then this is the opportunity for you!

* Own the brand marketing strategy that moves Pleo from ‘one of many’ to the undisputed choice for mid-market European finance leaders.
* Build and execute integrated brand campaigns from concept through to reporting — learning from what we’ve just launched, and pushing further.
* Create branded content that shows how financial services should be done. Content that recognizes the precision, rigor, and craft that finance leaders bring to their work.

* Own your budget and agency relationships — you’re the strategic partner they answer to.
* Measure what matters — working with Brand Intelligence, Integrated Marketing, Data, and MOps to track brand lift, earned media, consideration, and how brand work flows into pipeline and revenue.
* Set the benchmark for brand work in fintech — prove that category-defining campaigns come from strategic rigor and creative excellence working together. You’ll establish Pleo as the model for how brands should think about their audience, and show that understanding someone better than anyone else is a more powerful differentiator than any feature.
## **What you bring**
You’ll thrive in this role if you have:
* 10+ years in brand marketing (B2B or fintech might be helpful, but we care more about the thinking than the category)
* A portfolio of work that shows you’ve led campaigns from strategy through to execution — ideally integrated campaigns that work across multiple channels
* Strong stakeholder management skills — you can influence a room, sell an idea, and push back when something isn’t working
* Strategic thinking + execution mindset — you’re equally comfortable building a 6-month brand strategy and getting your hands dirty on day-to-day campaign work
* Comfort with ambiguity and pace — this is a growing company, and things move fast. You thrive in that
* Understanding of how brand and pipeline connect — you know that brand campaigns need to serve business growth, not just awareness
* A point of view on category dynamics — you can look at a market and spot where everyone’s getting it wrong
* A **strong understanding for when/how to localise** concepts, messaging & GTM campaigns across different markets.
* Fluency in one or more of our European markets is a bonus (not required, but helpful)
## **Why is this role a good fit for you**
This role is a good fit for you if:
* You want to reframe an entire category's conversation by competing on human insight rather than just feature parity.
* You thrive in a fast-paced, autonomous environment where you can build campaigns that serve as a 5-year foundation.
* You believe brand strategy must be grounded in audience understanding and directly drive business outcomes.
This role is not a good fit for you if:
* You prefer purely high-level strategy without getting hands-on with day-to-day campaign execution.
* You operate best in rigid, highly structured environments with slow moving pace and minimal ambiguity.
* You view brand marketing in isolation from performance data, pipeline metrics, and commercial growth.
## **How you’ll develop in this role**
In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:
* Map customer journeys across SMB, mid-market, and enterprise segments to identify brand opportunities.
* Develop a comprehensive European brand roadmap that builds on recent launch momentum.
* Develop a comprehensive European brand roadmap that builds on recent launch momentum.
## **The location**
Please note: We can hire on a hybrid set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.
## **Show me the benefits!**
* Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
* Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
* Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis
* 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).
* For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options
* We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far
* Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work
## **The interview process**
We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:
1. **Intro call:** A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
2. **Hiring Manager Interview:** A 45 minute chat to deep dive into your experience
3. **Challenge & Team Interview:** We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role
4. **Final Interview**: A final interview with a senior leader
Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!
Last time we hired for this role, we received a total vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:
* CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!
* Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.
* Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.
## **About your application**
* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.
* **Your data is safe.** When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.
* **Applying for multiple roles?** Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.
* **Reapplying.** If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

# IT Project Manager
**Poole, Dorset (hybrid working from home after successful training)**
**5 days a week | Monday – Friday 09:00 – 17:00**
**37.5 Hours a week**
**Main Purpose**
The IT Project Manager is responsible for the successful planning, coordination and delivery of technology and business transformation projects across Poole Bay Holdings.
The role will establish clear delivery plans, milestones, dependencies, ownership and governance, ensuring that projects progress in a controlled and transparent manner from initiation through to implementation and closure. Working closely with Business Analysis, Engineering, QA and business stakeholders, the Project Manager will ensure that scope, priorities, risks, issues and dependencies are understood and actively managed. They will be expected to distinguish between confirmed progress, forecast progress and unknowns, ensuring that project reporting provides an accurate representation of the delivery position.
The IT Project Manager will provide a clear and evidence-based view of project status, proactively identify threats to delivery and drive actions through to resolution. They will be responsible for maintaining effective project governance, ensuring decisions and actions have clear owners and deadlines, and escalating material risks or blockers when required.
The role requires a highly organised and delivery-focused individual who can operate effectively across multiple teams and complex initiatives while establishing the structure, accountability and communication required for successful delivery.
## Key Responsibilities
### Project Planning & Delivery
* Own the end-to-end planning and coordination of assigned technology and transformation projects.
* Establish clear project objectives, scope, deliverables, milestones and delivery plans.
* Develop and maintain detailed project plans showing activities, owners, dependencies, milestones and target dates.
* Coordinate delivery across Business Analysis, Engineering, QA, business teams and third-party suppliers.
* Establish and maintain the project critical path and proactively manage activities that could impact delivery.
* Ensure project dependencies are identified, understood, owned and actively managed.
* Track actual progress against agreed plans and milestones.
* Challenge progress and completion claims where appropriate and ensure project status is supported by evidence.
* Identify slippage early and establish appropriate recovery actions with delivery teams.
* Coordinate project activities through development, integration, testing, UAT, operational readiness and implementation.
* Ensure projects have clearly defined entry and exit criteria for significant delivery stages or gates.
* Support implementation, cutover and post-launch activities where required.
* Ensure projects are formally closed with outstanding actions, lessons learned and ownership clearly documented.
### Governance & Delivery Control
* Establish proportionate project governance appropriate to the scale, complexity and risk of each initiative.
* Maintain project RAID logs covering risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies.
* Ensure actions and decisions have clear owners and agreed completion dates.
* Maintain an accurate project decision log and ensure material decisions are appropriately documented.
* Establish appropriate project reporting and governance meetings.
* Produce concise and accurate project status reporting for Technology leadership and senior management.
* Maintain clear RAG reporting based on defined and consistently applied criteria.
* Escalate material risks, issues, dependencies and decisions promptly.
* Ensure project documentation and delivery evidence are maintained appropriately.
* Support effective change control when scope, requirements, priorities or delivery dates change.
* Maintain traceability between agreed scope, delivery plans and project outcomes.
* Ensure unresolved issues are visible rather than hidden within overall project status.
### Scope, Requirements & Change Control
* Work closely with Business Analysts to ensure project scope and requirements are sufficiently understood before being committed into delivery plans.
* Ensure changes to agreed scope are identified, assessed and controlled.
* Assess the delivery impact of proposed changes across schedule, resources, dependencies and risk.
* Prevent uncontrolled scope expansion and ensure material changes follow agreed governance.
* Ensure assumptions and unresolved business decisions are visible within project planning.
* Support prioritisation of requirements where delivery constraints require trade-offs.
* Ensure launch-critical requirements are clearly distinguished from subsequent roadmap activity.
* Maintain alignment between business requirements, delivery scope and project plans.
### Risk, Issue & Dependency Management
* Proactively identify risks to project delivery and ensure appropriate mitigation actions are established.
* Drive issues through to resolution rather than simply recording them.
* Identify cross-project, system, supplier and operational dependencies.
* Ensure dependencies have owners, required dates and clear consequences if they are not met.
* Escalate blockers when they cannot be resolved within the delivery team.
* Support contingency and recovery planning where significant delivery risks arise.
* Maintain clear visibility of decisions required from senior stakeholders.
* Ensure project risks are communicated objectively and without unsupported assumptions.
### Communication & Stakeholder Management
* Act as a central coordination point for assigned projects.
* Build effective working relationships across Technology and the wider Poole Bay Holdings business.
* Coordinate stakeholders across Technology, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Operations, Customer Service and other functions as required.
* Facilitate effective project meetings, ensuring clear decisions, actions, owners and deadlines.
* Communicate project status clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
* Adapt project communication appropriately for delivery teams, operational stakeholders and senior management.
* Challenge stakeholders constructively where actions, decisions or dependencies threaten delivery.
* Ensure stakeholders understand the impact of delays, changes and unresolved decisions.
* Coordinate third-party suppliers and delivery partners where required.
* Prepare project updates and executive reporting for the Group CTO and senior management.
### Delivery Team Coordination
* Work closely with Business Analysts, Lead/Senior Developers, Developers, QA and other delivery roles.
* Facilitate effective planning and coordination across the project lifecycle.
* Ensure teams have clarity around priorities, sequencing, dependencies and delivery expectations.
* Support backlog and delivery planning without taking ownership of business requirements or technical solution design.
* Coordinate resource requirements with Technology leadership.
* Identify capacity or capability constraints that could affect project delivery.
* Support effective hand-offs between requirements, development, QA, UAT and release.
* Help remove organisational and delivery blockers affecting the team.
* Promote accountability while maintaining a collaborative working environment.
### Systems & Process Improvement
* Use Jira and agreed project-management tools to maintain transparent delivery information.
* Ensure Jira and project reporting accurately reflect delivery status.
* Develop consistent project-management templates, controls and reporting practices.
* Identify opportunities to improve project delivery, governance and communication.
* Support implementation of consistent Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD) practices.
* Contribute to improving Technology portfolio and resource planning.
* Capture lessons learned and ensure relevant improvements are incorporated into future projects.
* Support the development of a consistent project and programme delivery framework across Poole Bay Holdings.

## Description
*This project is one of a number in competition for a studentship from the Faculty of Engineering and Design at the University of Bath. If successful, this studentship is expected to commence 04 October 2027.*
*An alternative start date may be possible if agreed with your intended supervisors and the Doctoral College.*
***Project Description***
| |
| --- |
| The transition towards low-carbon energy requires wind-energy technologies with increased efficiency, reliability and operational lifespan. Magnetic levitation offers potential for wind-energy systems by providing contactless rotor support, reducing friction, mechanical wear and maintenance requirements [1–4]. These characteristics make magnetic bearing technologies particularly relevant to the development of efficient and reliable wind-energy systems. However, magnetic levitation introduces additional challenges associated with rotor dynamics. The low mechanical damping associated with contactless support can increase susceptibility to vibration, instability and external disturbances. In active magnetic bearing systems, controllers are employed to regulate the rotor position and maintain contact-free operation [1, 3, 4]. Variations in rotational speed and aerodynamic loading introduce further dynamic uncertainties, requiring control strategies capable of maintaining satisfactory performance over a range of operating conditions [3–6]. This project will investigate advanced control strategies for magnetically levitated wind turbines, with particular emphasis on robust control. Mathematical models describing the dynamic behaviour of the magnetic levitation system will be developed and used to design control strategies for rotor stabilisation, vibration attenuation and disturbance rejection under uncertain and variable operating conditions. Particular attention will be given to the nonlinear electromagnetic forces associated with magnetic bearings. Suitable nonlinear system representations will be considered to account explicitly for these effects within the control design. Robust control methods for nonlinear systems, including Lur’e system formulations and LMI-based stability and control conditions, provide a framework for addressing nonlinearities and model uncertainty [7, 8]. The project provides an opportunity to combine renewable-energy applications with dynamic modelling and advanced control design. The outcomes will contribute to ongoing research on magnetically levitated wind turbines and provide a basis for the future implementation and experimental validation of advanced control strategies on prototype systems. |

An interest in dynamic systems, control, magnetic levitation systems and renewable-energy applications is desirable. Experience with mathematical modelling, system simulation, MATLAB/Simulink, Python or related computational tools would be advantageous. |
Applicants must have, or be about to obtain, a UK Honours degree 1st or 2.1, or international equivalent. A master’s level qualification would also be advantageous.

## 岗位信息
以下导读根据招聘原文整理,帮助你了解实际工作、要求和待遇;完整条件请核对下方原文。
### 岗位概况
Deepgram 招聘语音合成(TTS)研究总监,负责端到端掌管其文本转语音研究项目——包括研究战略、技术方向选择以及最终交付上线的模型。 这是一个亲力亲为的领导岗位:既要设定方向,也要深入细节,参与架构、实验、训练策略与评估的制定,同时搭建团队与运作模式。 工作地点为 London, UK,为全职雇主发布的远程岗位;远程并不代表全球均可申请。
### 工作职责
* 端到端掌管 TTS 研究与模型路线图,判断哪些技术方向能实质提升语音生成质量,包括昂贵且不显而易见的方向,并识别某条路线何时应当调整或终止。
* 推动神经音频建模、韵律与表现力、可控性、多语言语音、音色身份与一致性、数据与训练策略、后训练以及推理性能等方面的进展,并确保这些进展转化为可衡量的生产收益。
* 保持深度技术参与:审阅研究、质疑假设、设计实验、诊断模型失败,并亲自攻克最高杠杆的问题。
* 构建评估与基准体系,不仅说明模型是否改进,还要解释改进的原因——结合自动化指标与人类感知评估。
* 领导个人贡献者与技术负责人(tech lead manager)的混合团队:招聘并培养两类人才,维持极高的技术标准,将资深研究员培养为技术领导者,跨子团队设定方向,并把决策下放给最接近工作的人。
* 与工程和产品领导层就上线准备度协作,并在内部和外部代表 Deepgram 的 TTS 研究。
### 任职要求
* 在现代 TTS、语音生成或音频生成建模方面拥有深厚专长,并有亲自训练并改进大规模神经模型的过往记录。
* 精通现代语音生成技术栈,以及自然度、表现力、可控性、鲁棒性、音色一致性和推理成本等背后的开放问题。
* 有在真实不确定性下设定研究方向的经验:对实验排定优先级、分配算力与研究员时间,并终止无效路线。
* 有通过其他技术领导者(培养技术负责人或同等角色、跨子团队设定方向)领导研究员与研究工程师的经验,同时自身保持技术影响力。
* 将 AI 作为默认工作方式而非偶尔使用的工具:已围绕 AI 重建自己与团队的运作方式,并对它在语音研究中仍无法做到的事情有具体而切实的看法。
* 能够向产品、工程和高管受众清晰阐明复杂的技术权衡。
### 申请条件与限制
* 雇主发布的远程岗位,列明地点为 London, UK;远程并不意味着全球均可申请。
* employment\_type 为全职。

We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Data & Analytics team, working between home and our London office in Angel, Islington.
The Role
Data Science at PureGym influences some of the biggest decisions we make, from where we open our next gyms and how we price, to how we keep millions of members coming back.
Our models shape real decisions across retention, pricing, customer lifetime value and estate growth, with the impact showing up in the numbers our business runs on.
We're a small, experienced team that's great at turning good ideas into working solutions quickly. You'll join people who care about doing Data Science well, and you'll see your work used to make real commercial decisions throughout the business, not just admired in a notebook.
As our Senior Data Scientist, you'll take the technical lead on the modelling behind PureGym's spatial analytics capability.
You'll help us answer some of our most commercially important questions: where should we grow, how do our gyms fit within their local communities, and what drives the performance of different locations?
This is a role with significant ownership. You'll take spatial and location models from prototype through to trusted, production-ready assets, ensuring they're rigorous, explainable and capable of supporting confident investment and commercial decisions.
What you'll be doing
Own the spatial and location models that power our analytics tools, taking them from prototype through to maintained, well-documented production assets.
Build and evolve catchment, location and demand models that help us understand our markets, communities and opportunities for growth.
Partner closely with Property and Finance, translating commercial questions into analytical problems and ensuring our models deliver meaningful business value.
Rigorously validate models through out-of-time testing, leakage checks, sensitivity analysis and clear measures of uncertainty, ensuring every input genuinely reflects the information available at the point a decision is made.
Develop approaches for locations with limited historical data, using your technical judgement to determine when there is enough evidence to trust a result.
Work with Engineering and Data colleagues to turn model outputs into reusable, scalable data assets rather than one-off analysis or tables.
Partner with MLOps colleagues to deploy, monitor and retrain models, with clear ownership, versioning in MLflow and documented handover points.
Turn complex model outputs into clear, commercially relevant recommendations for senior stakeholders, including being transparent about uncertainty and where a model should, and should not, be used.
Evaluate external and third-party models with technical rigour, challenging assumptions and helping set the standard for how we assess them.
Contribute to shared development standards and peer review, sharing knowledge so that our capability can scale and no critical model is dependent on one person.
Help shape the future of spatial analytics at PureGym, identifying opportunities to improve our methods, tools and the commercial impact of our models.
The Person
You're an experienced Data Scientist with strong geospatial expertise who enjoys using complex data to solve real-world commercial problems where the answer isn't always obvious.
You're curious enough to question the data and rigorous enough to challenge an impressive-looking result when the evidence doesn't support it. You're also pragmatic: you understand that the best model isn't necessarily the most sophisticated one, but the one that's robust, explainable and genuinely helps people make a better decision.
You'll be:
Independent: You take ownership from problem definition and experimentation through to production, rather than stopping at proof of concept.
Commercially curious: You want to understand the decision behind the model and how your work ultimately creates value for the business.
Sceptical by default: You test assumptions, data and headline metrics before accepting them, whether they've come from an internal model or an external provider.
Pragmatic: You choose the simplest approach that produces a robust, reliable and explainable result rather than adding complexity for complexity's sake.
A strong collaborator: You enjoy solving problems alongside colleagues across Property, Finance, Engineering and Data.
A clear communicator: You're credible with senior non-technical stakeholders and can explain complex modelling, uncertainty and technical trade-offs in plain language.
Qualifications & Skills
The most important thing is that you combine strong Data Science fundamentals with genuine geospatial expertise and can demonstrate how you've used modelling to influence real-world decisions.
You'll bring:
A degree in a quantitative or geospatial discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Several years of applied Data Science experience, including building geospatial models that have been used to inform real-world decisions. Experience within retail, leisure, property or real estate would be particularly relevant.
Strong geospatial modelling expertise, for example spatial statistics, gravity and Huff-style models, network and isochrone analysis and spatial autocorrelation.
Proven experience taking at least one model from prototype through to production, with an understanding of what it takes to maintain and monitor it once live.
Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience writing version-controlled, tested and maintainable code.
Experience with the Python geospatial ecosystem and working with PySpark on Databricks.
Working knowledge of dbt, MLflow and production model deployment patterns.
Confidence using AI-assisted development tooling appropriately as part of the development lifecycle.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts and model outputs clearly to non-technical audiences.

Inzpire is looking for dynamic, proactive individuals with a ‘can do attitude’ who are capable of working within a military training environment with minimal supervision and are keen to contribute their own experience, suggesting ideas to continually improve the training delivery.

Additionally, if further sUAS and FPV experience has been gained after leaving military service in a civil capacity, this will also be considered favourably. * General Visual line of sight Certificate (GVC) or Remote Pilot Certificate (Level 1).
* Experienced in sUAS and FPV operations/flying hours (evidenced with Logbook)
* Experience in teaching or instructing others
* Valid Driving Licence.
* In date Passport.

* Military Experience – HM Forces Veteran with significant service or
* Civil UAS Operations Experience – at least a couple of logged UAS operations
* Letter of Recommendation from military chain of command or past civil UAS employer.
* sUAS and or FPV Instructional Experience.
* Instructor Qualifications: accredited to Level 3 Award in Education are highly desirable, but other instructional qualifications will be considered including Defence Train the Trainer (DTTT) or Aircrew Instructor Course (AIC), CFS qualifications etc.

* Extant Security Clearance (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV) highly desirable.
* Familiarity with MAA RA 1600 series.

# Trading and Liquidity Strategy Lead
**About Quidax**
Quidax is where money meets limitless possibilities. We’re making it super easy for individuals, businesses, and fintechs in Africa to access crypto. Our goal? Providing real value for our customers today while shaping the future of money.
**About the Role**
We're looking for a hands-on Trading and Liquidity Strategy Lead who understands crypto markets from doing the work. You know how to read an Order Book, find liquidity, manage a position and explain what a trade actually earned after costs.
You'll help make sure customers can trade at competitive prices, with enough liquidity and reliable execution. That matters whether they're using Instant Swap, trading on our Order Book, working with the OTC Desk or building on our APIs.
A big part of your role will be looking at our markets and asking:
* **"Can someone actually trade at that price?"**
* **"Why is liquidity thinning out?"**
* **"What are we earning after costs, and what risk are we carrying?"**
You'll report directly to the **Chief Financial Officer (CFO)**. We want someone who spots problems early, makes sound trading decisions and follows through until things work better.
**What You’ll Be Owning**
**Keep Our Markets Healthy**
* Monitor spreads, Order Book depth, fill rates, time to fill and slippage across our core pairs, especially USDT/NGN.
* Investigate stale quotes, one-sided liquidity and unusual price moves. Work out whether the issue is market demand, available funds, a liquidity provider or a system problem.
* Compare our pricing with executable prices on relevant markets. Know when a local premium makes sense and when our own quotes need attention.
**Find Liquidity & Execute Well**
* Source and execute trades through approved exchanges and counterparties, choosing the right venue, order type and size for the trade.
* Support liquidity and execution for the OTC Desk and our trading products. Know when to split an order, use a limit order or source an OTC quote.
* Assess cross-exchange and arbitrage opportunities after trading fees, slippage, funding and transfer costs. Check that both sides can actually execute and settle.
**Make Pricing & Market Making Work Better**
* Review our quotes and spreads against market conditions, inventory and the full cost of execution. Recommend changes that balance competitive pricing with sustainable margins.
* Work with market makers and liquidity providers on reliable two-sided quotes, useful depth and consistent availability.
* Check whether liquidity partners are improving execution, not just adding volume. Address weak performance and recommend better sources where needed.
**Stay on Top of Positions & Risk**
* Track trading inventory, open orders, unsettled trades and counterparty exposure. Execute approved hedges and rebalancing trades within agreed limits.
* Work with Treasury Ops and Finance on funding, settlement, reconciliation, realised and unrealised P&L. Investigate differences rather than carrying them forward unexplained.
* Escalate limit breaches, pricing errors and suspected market abuse promptly. Keep clear trade records and follow approval controls, even when the market is moving quickly.
**Turn Market Insight into Better Operations**
* Give the CFO a clear view of market health, execution costs, P&L and emerging risks, with specific recommendations and follow-through.
* Work with Product and Engineering on price checks, liquidity alerts and trading tools that help us catch problems earlier.
* Document trading decisions, incident responses and handovers. Share what works so good execution does not depend on one person being available.
**Within your first 3 months, we'd like you to:**
* Understand our trading flows, liquidity sources, positions and controls well enough to operate confidently within your mandate.
* Establish a baseline for spreads, depth, fill rates, slippage and trading costs across priority pairs.
* Identify the biggest gaps in pricing, liquidity or execution and agree an action plan with the CFO.
* Deliver at least one measurable improvement in execution quality, net spread or liquidity availability without increasing exposure beyond agreed limits.
* Put practical monitoring, escalation and handover routines in place with the relevant teams.
We'll give you the context and support to understand Quidax. We expect you to bring the trading experience and judgement to put that context to work.
**Biggest Challenges You’ll Tackle**
Here's what will keep you busy and hopefully make the role fun:
* **Knowing what's really executable:** A good-looking price means little if there isn't enough depth, funds are in the wrong place or settlement is uncertain.
* **Keeping up with local and global markets:** USDT/NGN doesn't move only because crypto moves. You'll need to understand local fiat liquidity and demand too.
* **Balancing price, profit and risk:** Tighter spreads can help customers, but not every trade is worth taking. You'll need to know where the economics stop making sense.
* **Acting quickly without cutting corners:** Markets won't wait for perfect information. You'll need to make clear decisions, respect limits and know when to escalate.
* **Fixing the cause:** When a trade fails or liquidity disappears, the job isn't finished when you flag it. You'll help find the cause and prevent it happening again.
**What We’re Looking For**
We're more interested in the decisions you've made and the results you can explain than a long list of trading terms. You might be a great fit if:
* You've executed and managed crypto trades across multiple exchanges, ideally at an exchange, market maker or OTC desk.
* You've been accountable for trading positions, execution quality and P&L. You can explain your own decisions, including the ones that didn't work.
* You understand Order Book mechanics, Maker and Taker fees, order types, slippage, market impact and inventory risk in practice.
* You're familiar with NGN/stablecoin markets and can explain how local liquidity, FX movements and settlement constraints affect pricing.
* You're comfortable working with liquidity providers and counterparties, checking quotes and following a trade through to settlement.
* You can use spreadsheets and trading data to calculate costs, check P&L and investigate an execution problem.
* You stay calm when markets move, communicate clearly and raise problems early. You don't need someone to tell you when something deserves attention.
Experience with exchange APIs, SQL, Python or trading automation is a plus. Good trading judgement is essential.
Have you:
* Improved liquidity or execution on a trading pair?
* Executed a large trade without giving away the margin through slippage?
* Caught a pricing or exposure problem before it became a bigger loss?
Tell us about it. What did you notice? What did you do? What changed? We're interested in the work you personally owned.
**Reporting Line**
You'll report directly to the **Chief Financial Officer (CFO)** and work closely with the Markets Operations team, Treasury Ops, Finance, Product, Engineering and Compliance.
If you're the kind of person who sees a wide spread and immediately wants to understand what's behind it, we'd love to meet you.
**Why Quidax?**
This isn’t just a leadership role, it’s a chance to shape the future of crypto in Africa and beyond. If you're looking for a high-impact role where you can build, scale, and lead in a fast-moving industry, Quidax is the place to be.
