Harness Engineering exists to break that bottleneck: engineering the environment that steers agents toward correct, maintainable, well-architected output so that quality is enforced by the system, not re-audited by a person on every change. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness), and we're building a dedicated Harness Engineering team to own it. # Data Analyst — Energy Retail (Oil & Gas)
IT - London, Greater London
---
About the role
A hands-on analyst for a consumer energy business: pay-as-you-go cooking gas (LPG) delivered to hundreds of thousands of households in fast-growing emerging markets. You own the analysis end to end — framing the question, getting the data, building the numbers and defending them in front of the people who will act on them. You work directly with commercial, operations, finance and management, and with our founders — no account manager in between.
You join our energy data team, alongside a senior data scientist and a data & BI engineer. A meaningful part of the work starts in raw tables, meter logs, payment exports and field-operations files rather than in a tidy warehouse.
We do not require you to come from oil & gas. The business model is much closer to a prepaid mobile operator than to a fuel station: customers top up credit with mobile money, consume in small amounts, and every unit used is recorded by a smart meter. Experience at mobile network operators, telecoms, mobile money or fintech, utilities with prepaid metering, pay-as-you-go solar, and similar high-volume B2C businesses is directly relevant.
What the work looks like
Each customer home has a stove, a smart meter and a gas cylinder owned and maintained by the company. Customers pay only for the gas they use, topping up as little as a single meal’s worth through mobile money, and local technicians replace cylinders before they run out. That produces rich data — consumption, top-ups, cylinder swaps, deliveries, meter events — and commercial questions to match: which customers stay and why, what a customer is worth, where the network makes or loses money, and what to do about it.
Scope
* Customer analytics — acquisition, activation, retention and churn, cohort behaviour, revenue and margin per household, lifetime value against the cost of installation
* Consumption and top-up behaviour — frequency and size of top-ups, usage patterns, seasonality, early signs that a customer is about to go dormant
* Pricing and promotion analysis — the effect of price, top-up incentives and campaigns on usage and margin, measured against proper baselines and control groups
* Field operations and unit economics — cylinder swap and delivery efficiency, depot and area performance, technician productivity, cost to serve per household
* Forecasting gas demand, cylinder logistics and revenue by area, to support supply, stock and expansion decisions
* Anomaly and fraud detection — meter tampering, consumption that does not match cylinder swaps, payment irregularities, unusual field activity
* Reporting with single agreed definitions where commercial, operations and finance count customers, revenue or volume differently
* Messy data as the normal case: meter connectivity gaps, delayed payment records, re-assigned devices, data from more than one country and system
Requirements

# Head of IT and Infrastructure
London
## **About Red Badger**
We’re a tech and product consultancy, building enterprise software products for blue chip companies, multinationals and PLC’s. The best bit about Red Badger is; of course; the team. We are a diverse group made up of 22 different nationalities, speaking 17 different languages. Headquartered in London we also have offices in Leeds and Cape Town and Australia and New Zealand
## **Role Overview**
As the Head of IT & Infrastructure, you will have end-to-end ownership of Red Badger’s global IT landscape. This is a dynamic, high-impact role that blends strategic leadership with hands-on execution. You will ensure our multi-location staff enjoy frictionless, secure, and reliable technology experiences every day.
You will manage our identity stack, cloud networking, SaaS ecosystem, device fleet, and compliance standards (ISO 27001 & Cyber Essentials) across our four hubs (London, Leeds, Cape Town, and Australia & New Zealand). As Red Badger grows, you will build and lead a distributed IT team, travelling to regional hubs when necessary to establish local infrastructure.

#### **1. Global Infrastructure, Identity & Access Management**
* Administer, optimise, and secure our cloud-first identity and access ecosystem, centered around Google Workspace and JumpCloud.
* Implement and enforce modern zero-trust architecture, maintaining Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM provisioning across all company applications.
* Manage, maintain, and upgrade physical networks across all locations, including firewalls, Wi-Fi infrastructure, and cloud RADIUS setup.
#### **2. SaaS Ecosystem & Vendor Management**
* Act as the commercial and administrative owner for Red Badger’s SaaS stack (100+ applications).
* Oversee license management, vendor renewals, billing optimization, and procurement to ensure cost efficiency and compliance.
#### **3. User Support, AV & Daily Operations**
* Provide high-touch 1st-line and escalated support to all Red Badger staff across time zones (London, Leeds, Cape Town, Australia & New Zealand).
* Administer and maintain office Audio-Visual systems, specifically Google Meet Hardware rooms, ensuring seamless hybrid collaboration.
* Establish IT onboarding/offboarding workflows that guarantee day-one readiness for new hires worldwide.
#### **4. Device Fleet Management (MDM)**
* Manage the full lifecycle of Red Badger's endpoint fleet (laptops and mobile devices), including procurement, deployment, patch management, security policy enforcement, and eco-friendly disposal via MDM tools.
#### **5. Governance, Security & Compliance**
* Lead, gain, and maintain key industry certifications, including Cyber Essentials / Cyber Essentials Plus and ISO 27001.
* Take responsibility for ensuring data retention policies are in place and align to current legislation.
* Conduct regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, and access reviews across all systems.
* Create, update, and enforce IT security policies and disaster recovery procedures.
#### **6. Global Growth & Team Leadership**
* Support business growth in regional hubs (Leeds, Cape Town, Australia & New Zealand) by defining local IT setups and travelling on-site during initial rollouts or expansions.
* Hire, mentor, and build a high-performing distributed IT support team as headcount grows in regional hubs.

* Identity Architecture: Deep hands-on experience setting up and managing SSO, SCIM provisioning, and cloud RADIUS.
* Networking & Hardware: Solid experience managing enterprise network equipment (UniFi, Meraki, or similar), firewalls, Wi-Fi, and Google Meet AV setups.
* Compliance: Proven track record in achieving and maintaining ISO 27001 and Cyber Essentials compliance.
* Device Management: Strong experience managing Apple (macOS/iOS) fleets using JumpCloud MDM.
* Vendor & Budget Ownership: Comfortable managing vendor relationships, negotiating software contracts, and controlling SaaS spending.
* Adaptability & Mobility: Willingness to travel to international hubs (Cape Town, Australia & New Zealand) and UK offices (Leeds) when establishing new infrastructure.

* Service-Minded Culture: Outstanding interpersonal skills and a empathy-first attitude toward supporting team members.
* Pragmatic Security: Ability to balance robust security practices with employee productivity and frictionless workflows.
* Autonomy: Self-motivated and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where you own outcomes from strategy down to execution.

We make sure our team is well looked after with generous salaries and a great benefits package which includes:
* Annual £2,000 training budget
* Enhanced pension with employer contribution of up to 5% of your salary
* Group Life Insurance
* Income Replacement Benefit
* Critical Illness Cover
* Private Medical Insurance
* Your choice of hardware and mobile phone
* £1,000 home-office set up budget and contribution to home broadband
* Matched (pre-tax) charity GAYE donations
* Cycle to work
* Enhanced parental leave

1. **People people** We respect and care for each other, giving us the space to be our true selves.
2. **Find a way** We’re comfortable with uncertainty, and want to take ownership for outcomes, which we are proactive in delivering.
3. **Always learning** We’re curious. It’s how we learn and grow as individuals, continuously testing and improving what we do, and how we do it.

5. **Collaborative**We are united by our desire to get to the best ideas. We are generous with our knowledge, actively listen to each other, and are open minded.

Red Badger is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment, and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. **Location:** Coventry Police Station, Coventry, with travel to head office as required **Salary:** £29,540 per annum **Hours:** Full-time, Monday to Friday **Contract:** To be confirmed
## About the Role
RSR is a public safety and enterprise security recruitment specialist, supporting organisations that make a real difference to people’s lives.
We are recruiting a **Domestic Abuse Practitioner** to join an Early Intervention Project based at Coventry Police Station. This is an opportunity to provide vital early support to individuals affected by domestic abuse, helping them access the advice, protection and practical assistance they need to move forward safely.
Working in partnership with the police and local support services, you will act as a first point of contact for individuals experiencing domestic abuse, providing crisis intervention, risk assessments, safety planning, advocacy and ongoing emotional and practical support.
The role has a particular focus on supporting individuals from Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic (BAME) and refugee communities, including those affected by forced marriage, female genital mutilation (FGM), honour-based abuse and barriers to accessing public services.
## Key Responsibilities
* Provide an immediate, trauma-informed response to individuals affected by domestic abuse, offering advice, emotional support and safety planning.
* Complete detailed needs assessments and risk assessments, developing and reviewing individual support plans.
* Work closely with Coventry Police to identify suitable referrals, assess needs and communicate outcomes and recommended actions.
* Manage a caseload, providing one-to-one support, advocacy, guidance and group interventions where appropriate.
* Support individuals to access housing, homelessness services, welfare benefits, legal advice, healthcare and other relevant services.
* Help individuals understand their rights and options for legal protection for themselves and their children.
* Identify and respond to safeguarding concerns, including making appropriate child protection and MARAC referrals.
* Build effective working relationships with police officers, statutory services, charities and other partner agencies.
* Maintain accurate case records, confidential files, monitoring information and performance data.
* Promote awareness of the Early Intervention Project and develop positive relationships with external agencies.
* Ensure all support is delivered in a non-judgemental, culturally sensitive and empowering manner.
## Essential Experience and Requirements
**Candidates must be able to demonstrate the following:**
* Previous experience supporting individuals affected by domestic abuse, forced marriage (FM), female genital mutilation (FGM) and/or honour-based abuse (HBA).
* Experience providing practical and emotional support to women and children affected by abuse.
* Experience advising and advocating on issues including housing, homelessness, benefits, legal matters and social welfare.
* A good understanding of domestic abuse, relevant legislation, safeguarding procedures and referral pathways.
* Experience identifying safeguarding concerns and making appropriate referrals for children and vulnerable adults.
* Experience developing and maintaining effective relationships with external agencies.
* The ability to communicate fluently in **at least one of the following languages:** Urdu, Hindi, Mirpuri, Punjabi, Gujarati, Bengali, Farsi, Pashtu or an African language, particularly Somali.
* A full, current driving licence, access to a vehicle and business-use insurance.
* A clear Enhanced DBS check.
* Strong communication, listening, organisation and administration skills, with good IT literacy.
* The ability to manage a demanding caseload, work under pressure and use initiative while maintaining professional boundaries.
Candidates should also demonstrate an understanding of the additional barriers faced by BAME and refugee communities, including discrimination, cultural pressures, immigration-related concerns and No Recourse to Public Funds (NRPF).
## Qualifications and Training
A good general standard of education is required. Candidates should have undertaken relevant training in domestic abuse, honour-based abuse, forced marriage and No Recourse to Public Funds. Training will be provided where necessary, and successful candidates must be willing to undertake any outstanding training.
A recognised counselling qualification or relevant professional qualification, such as an NVQ, would be advantageous.
## Personal Attributes
The successful candidate will be:
* Empathetic, approachable and non-judgemental.
* Committed to empowering individuals to make informed choices and regain control of their lives.
* Sensitive to cultural differences and committed to equality, diversity and anti-discriminatory practice.
* Able to remain calm and professional in stressful or crisis situations.
* Respectful of confidentiality, privacy and professional boundaries.
* Flexible, organised and comfortable working independently and as part of a multi-agency team.

Apply today to be considered for this full-time opportunity to help individuals access the support and protection they need to live free from abuse and fear.

Description
## About The Role
The Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT) launched its Blue Recovery work in 2021: a major initiative to deliver transformational environmental change in the UK. There is growing evidence showing the significant role that wetlands can play in four critical areas: storing carbon, reducing flooding, benefiting wellbeing and improving water quality, but these benefits are not widely understood.
WWT has brought together a consortium of sector leading organisations to help unlock and demonstrate the value of wetland creation, facilitating the creation of a network of wetlands that will deliver lasting impact and act as a catalyst for wider action. Its approach draws on the model used by the Sustainable Markets Initiative launched by our Patron, HRH King Charles III.
At the heart of WWT’s proposals is an ambition to create and restore 100,000 hectares of healthy wetland in the UK, conceived of as four networks:
* A carbon storage network, consisting of wetlands to sequester and store carbon
* A flood management network, consisting of wetland features to reduce flooding
* An urban wellbeing network, consisting of wetlands to improve wellbeing
* A water treatment network, consisting of wetlands to support biodiversity
This Blue Recovery will make a vital contribution to the UK’s environmental and climate change goals.
**Role Outline**
You will be responsible for working with WWT’s Blue Recovery Leaders Group to drive forward this partnership leading to the delivery of projects that fulfil WWT’s Blue Recovery workstream. By building and maintaining close relationships with the Blue Recovery Leader’s Group drawn from industries including the water, construction, finance, agriculture and engineering sectors, you will support the group to develop projects that demonstrate the multiple benefits that wetlands provide to society.
You will act as WWT’s main lead on supporting the Blue Recovery Leaders Group and work with them to develop project ideas and proposals that fulfil WWT’s strategic ambitions. You will liaise between our Philanthropy & Partnerships, UK Programmes and Conservation Evidence Teams, coordinating input from them to ensure successful delivery of The Blue Recovery Leaders contribution towards WWT’s Strategic Plan.

If this sounds like you then we would very much like to hear from you. Come and join us in delivering our vision of a world where healthy wetland nature thrives and enriches lives.

We’re WWT, and we’re on a mission to restore the super-powered ecosystems we call wetlands. There’s never been a more important moment for our work, and we’ve got some phenomenal people on the case.

Relief-to-Hire makes that a product: hospitals try before they hire and pay a placement fee only when a hire happens. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of the management team, you'll own the Relief-to-Hire P&L (placement revenue, contribution margin, and the investment decisions behind them) and be accountable for making Roo the way veterinary practices hire, instead of a job ad or a recruiter.

Until now it has been run by a cross-functional squad rather than a dedicated owner; in January 2027 it becomes its own business unit with a P&L, a budget and a GM. You'll lead a small placement team directly, set priorities for a dedicated product manager and growth analyst, and get much of your leverage from design, engineering, lifecycle marketing and data partners you don't manage. * Grow Relief-to-Hire faster than the relief marketplace it's built on.

## About the Role
We're looking for a Senior Growth Marketing Manager to grow Roo's business with independent veterinary hospitals. You'll own hospital growth across the full funnel: how practice owners and managers discover Roo, why they sign up, what gets them to post and fill their first shift, and what keeps them coming back.
You'll be accountable for bringing hospitals onto Roo and turning them into active, repeat customers, with success measured by hospitals that activate and stay active alongside sign-ups and leads. As the business unit's first dedicated growth marketer, you'll shape the growth strategy, own the growth budget and measurement, and lead testing across the hospital journey.
You'll report to the GM of Independent Hospitals, with a dotted line to the Marketing leadership and be part of Roo's marketing guild, which owns craft standards for marketing across the company.
## Responsibilities
**Growth Strategy & Planning**
* **Shape the strategy.** Shape the hospital growth strategy with the GM and product, setting goals for acquisition, activation, reactivation, and expansion, plus acquisition cost and payback targets tied to hospitals that fill shifts and keep posting.
* **Own the budget.** Own the hospital growth budget and channel mix, allocating spend by market tier based on where shifts are most likely to fill, and deciding what to scale, what to cut, and what should wait.
**Acquisition**
* **Own hospital channels.** This covers both acquisition motions: B2B lead generation and account-based campaigns with sales, and direct-to-practice-manager acquisition through paid search and social. It also covers direct mail, referrals, sponsorships, buying-group partnerships, and SEO and AEO priorities, partnering with brand on the build.
* **Own hospital acquisition campaigns.** Own hospital-only acquisition campaigns, and bring the acquisition layer to company-wide campaigns led by the brand team.
* **Partner on events.** Partner with the brand and community teams on conferences, industry events, and webinars, bringing the hospital targeting and shaping the follow-up that turns attendees into active hospitals.
* **Target the right hospitals.** Partner with sales, Rev Ops, and analytics on hospital targeting and lead scoring, so marketing, the field team, and automated outreach focus on the hospitals most likely to fill and grow.
* **Own the field handoff.** Set lead routing, handoff SLAs, and the rules for which hospitals get a Hospital Success Partner (HSP) and which get AI-driven outreach.
**Activation & Conversion**
* **Get hospitals to first fill.** Own the CRO backlog, test roadmap, and first-fill playbook across the hospital journey, from landing pages and sign-up to approval and first shift posted, partnering with product on the sign-up and first-shift experience.
* **Partner on product experiments.** Work with product and growth analysts to develop, launch, and evaluate A/B tests and product experiments, such as homepage banners and headline tests.
* **Find where hospitals drop off.** Diagnose where and why hospitals drop off, using funnel data alongside what practice owners, managers, and the field team say, and turn what you learn into fixes.
* **Shape activation journeys.** Partner with the lifecycle team on onboarding and activation journeys, bringing the audience insight, goals, and offers that shape them.
* **Make the incentive case.** Partner with the pricing team on incentive strategy: which hospitals get one, what offer, and the payback against hospital LTV.
* **Brief the creative.** Partner with brand on campaign creative, landing pages, and website updates, bringing clear briefs, audience insight, and performance learnings that shape the work.
* **Sharpen the message.** Partner with product marketing and brand on hospital positioning and messaging, and bring channel and test results back to sharpen it.
**Retention & Expansion**
* **Win back dormant hospitals.** Own the reactivation campaign for dormant, churned, and unfilled-shift hospitals, partnering with the lifecycle team on the journeys and messaging that bring them back to Roo.
* **Grow existing accounts.** Build expansion programs that help hospitals use Roo more often and book across more roles, such as adding veterinary technicians.
**Measurement & Insights**
* **Own the numbers.** Own hospital growth measurement, including the model that tracks acquisition cost by channel, cohort activation, fill rates, lifetime value, and payback, the holdout standard every program is measured against, and the attribution and tests with clear success criteria that show what each program actually drove.
* **Report and adjust.** Read results honestly, move investment toward what's working, and share progress, spend, and learnings with business unit and marketing leadership.
### How This Role Works With the Team
This role sits at the center of the business unit and works through others. You'll partner with the Hospital Success Partner field team on who to target and how leads get routed, and with product and growth analysts on experiments and the sign-up and first-shift experience. You'll also work with product marketing on positioning, lifecycle on activation and reactivation journeys, pricing on first-fill incentives, analytics on targeting and measurement, and brand and community on creative, the website, events, and webinars. Because fill depends on veterinary professional supply, you'll work closely with the Veterinary Marketplace business unit so hospital demand and supply grow in the same markets. You'll bring these teams together around a shared growth plan.
### What Success Looks Like
In your first year, you will:
* Grow hospital acquisition against plan and within budget.
* Increase the share of new hospitals that post and fill their first shift.
* Grow the number of hospitals posting regularly on Roo.
* Bring dormant hospitals back to active use, in partnership with the lifecycle team.
* Set a clear measure for every channel and move investment toward what works.
* Build a testing roadmap and first-fill playbook the business unit runs on.

* **Full-funnel growth experience.** Experience in growth or performance marketing to small businesses, ideally at a marketplace or vertical SaaS company. You've owned a budget and a channel mix.

* **B2B channel range.** Hands-on with paid search and social, sponsorships, partnerships, referrals and direct mail, and you know when to cut a channel. Bonus if you've run account-based plays for high-priority accounts alongside broad demand gen.
* **Root-cause thinking.** You've diagnosed why customers sign up and don't activate, and improved conversion by fixing the root cause.
* **Field sales partnership.** You've worked alongside a sales or account team on lead scoring, routing and handoffs, and you can tell which touches actually move the number.

* **Startup-ready.** You thrive in ambiguity and enjoy building programs from scratch.
* **AI fluency.** You use AI to scale your own output and have a view on where agents can replace manual outreach.
* **Bonus.** Experience in veterinary medicine, healthcare, marketplaces, or staffing is a plus.
### Why Roo

### About the role (from employer)
### **Building the Future of Open Finance**
Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.
### **The team**
Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.
Join our Product and Regulatory Legal team, embedded with Kraken's Product, Design and Engineering teams to ship novel products and experiences that accelerate the global adoption of crypto. We are a tight, experienced group of lawyers from a diverse range of tradfi, fintech and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice, partnering directly with Product, senior leadership and Compliance to chart clear, defensible paths to launch and to keep our licensed entities running smoothly.
This is a senior product-facing legal role for the European Union. You will be the lawyer the business trusts on questions that cut across several regimes at once: for example, a single product such as a tokenised equity, a card, or an institutional custody and prime brokerage service can touch the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive ("MiFID II"), the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCA"), the Payment Services Directive ("PSD2"), the Electronic Money Directive ("EMD2") and banking rules at the same time. You will bring clarity on which regime applies, what it requires, and how to launch within it.
### **The opportunity**
Reporting to the Head of Product Legal, you will act as a senior legal adviser to European leadership on new products, licensing structure and regulatory strategy.
* Own cross-functional product counselling for European Union launches from discovery to design, launch and iteration, giving Product, Engineering, Compliance and leadership decision-ready advice with clear options and risk trade-offs
* Advise on the regulatory perimeter and classification of new offerings across MiFID II and the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation ("MiFIR"), MiCA, the European Market Infrastructure Regulation ("EMIR"), payment services and electronic money rules, and banking regulation, including where an instrument or service falls between regimes (for example tokenised securities, crypto-asset derivatives, margin and financing, and stablecoin-linked products)
* Advise on payments and electronic money offerings, including the Krak card and account propositions, safeguarding, open banking and account-access obligations, and the developing Payment Services Directive 3 and Payment Services Regulation framework
* Advise on banking-related questions that arise in the European Union, including bank partnerships and sponsor-bank arrangements, deposit-taking and lending perimeter questions, the Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive, and the interaction of these rules with our custody, prime brokerage and financing products
* Monitor and interpret European Union legislative and supervisory developments, take part in consultations and industry association work where appropriate, and translate their significance for the business proactively
* Draft and negotiate client-facing terms and conditions, taking clear, business-aligned positions
* Act as gatekeeper for European Union outside counsel engagements: scope the work, estimate and manage cost, and sign off before matters go externally
* Mentor and develop more junior lawyers in the team, set quality standards for plain-English, risk-based advice, and act as a senior sounding board for colleagues across the Regulatory Legal team

## About the Position
These projects are open to students worldwide, but have no funding attached. Therefore, the successful applicant will be expected to fund tuition fees at the relevant level (home or international) and any applicable additional research costs. Please consider this before applying.
Computer vision systems powered by deep learning are central to many modern applications, ranging from autonomous vehicles and medical imaging to industrial automation and precision agriculture. At the heart of these systems lies the image encoder, which transforms raw image data into compact representations for tasks such as classification and object detection. However, state-of-the-art encoders are often computationally intensive, demanding substantial energy and hardware resources for both training and deployment.
This project aims to develop lightweight image encoder architectures that support energy-efficient AI for computer vision, particularly in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and Internet of Things (IoT) systems. While current research has largely focused on maximizing performance through increasingly large models, it frequently overlooks the environmental and practical limitations of such approaches.
The proposed research will explore complexity reduction through intelligent image pre-processing. Many images contain large areas of redundant or semantically irrelevant data that contribute little to the task at hand. This project seeks to develop techniques for efficiently compressing images while preserving the semantically relevant information required for downstream tasks. The core hypothesis is that reducing input data enables the development of smaller, more efficient image encoders with minimal loss in accuracy.
The expected outcome is a set of compact, high-performing image encoders suitable for deployment in low-power environments. This work will also contribute to the advancement of sustainable AI systems, addressing the growing demand for environmentally responsible and accessible computer vision technologies.

## About the Position
Background: Brain tumours are among the leading causes of cancer-related deaths in children. While surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy have increased survival rates these tumours still cause many deaths among patients. In addition, many survivors suffer long-term side effects from these treatments. Thus, greater understanding of the molecular basis of disease in these tumours is needed in order to improve patient treatment and survival. Rab GTPases are a large family of small GTPases that control vesicle budding, motility and fusion in all eukaryotes. Many studies have linked Rab dysfunction with cancer progression and metastasis, although their role in paediatric brain tumour has yet to be defined. In other tumour types, Rab dysfunction is associated with increased protease secretion, growth factor receptor recycling to the plasma membrane and exosome secretion, all of which are linked to poor prognosis and disease progression. The aim of this project is to test the hypothesis that specific Rab GTPases regulate vesicle trafficking pathways that contribute to the pathogenesis of paediatric brain tumours focusing on ependymoma and high-grade gliomas (including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), anaplastic astrocytoma and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG)). Environment: Drs Hume and Coyle already co-supervise two PhD students investigating the involvement of disordered membrane transport in the paediatric brain cancer medulloblastoma. Drs Hume and Coyle's labs are focussed on understanding the role of Rabs in membrane trafficking pathways and the basis and treatment of paediatric brain tumours. This project offers an opportunity to address an important biological question with the aim of improving the treatment for children diagnosed with these devastating tumours. Aims: 1. To identify Rabs whose expression is linked to outcome in paediatric brain tumours; ependymoma and high-grade glioma. 2. To identify the role of these Rabs in tumour cell biology and pathology. 3. To inhibit the function of specific Rab GTPases and look at their effect on tumour cell proliferation and metastasis. The project will last up to 4 years and will be available full-time. Both Home and International students are welcome to apply. Applications accepted all year round. Self-funded PhD students only.

# Adaptive Information Allocation in Machine Learning
Ph.D·University of Birmingham·School of Computer Science·United Kingdom
Position type

Level

Language

## About the Position
Stochastic gradient methods represent a key computational engine of large-scale modern machine learning. To estimate gradient directions, they sample training data uniformly at random, independently of their informational value. However, real-world datasets are heterogeneous, containing noise, outliers, imbalance, and unknown varying levels of deviations from the i.i.d. assumption. Consequently, gradient estimates obtained from uniformly sampled examples can vary dramatically in quality, leading to inefficient optimisation, unnecessary computation, and reduced robustness. This project addresses a foundational question in machine learning: How should a learning system allocate its stochastic computational effort across data of unequal informational value? We propose a new framework in which the sampling process in stochastic optimisation is not fixed, but learned jointly with model parameters - that is, an adaptive data selection or learned sampling policy. This transforms stochastic gradient descent into a coupled learning system consisting of: (1) a model learning process driven by stochastic gradients, and (2) a data selection process that adapts to data imperfections and to the evolving state of learning. The key idea is that learning efficiency is determined not only by model capacity, but by how the optimisation process allocates attention across training data. The project will develop a principled theory, algorithms, and analysis of this coupled system. Specifically, its scope includes the following: develop a PAC-Bayes theory for learning under adaptive data selection; identify the conditions under which adaptive sampling provably improves optimisation efficiency, robustness, and generalisation; design scalable algorithms for joint optimisation of model parameters and sampling policies; evaluate performance in noisy, imbalanced, heterogeneous, and non-i.i.d. data regimes. The expected outcome is a new theoretical and algorithmic foundation for stochastic optimisation in which computational effort is allocated adaptively according to the informational value of the data. This perspective provides a principled route to more data-efficient, robust, and computationally scalable machine learning systems operating in realistic heterogeneous environments. * SC cleared, active SC or SC eligible.
* Demonstrable experience designing and shipping interaction design for complex digital services.

* Able to explain design decisions to stakeholders and collaborate across disciplines.

Personal data is all information that can be directly or indirectly linked to a living, physical person. Examples of personal data are: name, e-mail address, telephone number and IP address. Processing of personal data is any automated use of personal data - such as collecting, creating, analyzing, sharing, and deleting personal data.
There are laws and regulations on how companies may process personal data, so-called data protection laws. Different data protection laws apply to different types of use of personal data, and in different parts of the world. An example of a data protection law that is relevant for our use of your personal data, as described in this privacy policy, is the EU Data Protection Regulation (2016/679, "GDPR").
Most obligations under the GDPR apply to the so-called data controller. A data controller is the entity that decides for which purposes personal data will be processed, and how the processing will be executed. The data controller can use a so-called data processor. A data processor is an entity that is only allowed to process personal data as instructed by the data controller, and may not use the personal data for its own purposes.

You lead the Privacy squad and report to the VP Product.
Your mission: monetize as much traffic as possible within privacy rules. You turn standards and laws into clear product rules. You defend the compliant interpretation that protects our publishers’ revenue, and you never apply a rule more strictly than it requires.
##### Your key responsibilities
**1. Consent Engine & Frameworks**
* Own the roadmap of the FastCMP signal engine: IAB TCF, GPP, GPC (Global Privacy Control), Google Consent Mode and US privacy signals.
* Define jurisdictions: which framework and which default behavior apply in each country.
* Deliver each new standard version on time, on web, app and CTV.
**2. Rules Every Channel Can Apply**
* Translate each standard and each law into product specifications for each channel: Actirise, Viously, Meetscale Web, App and CTV.
* Own the compliance checklist that every consent-related initiative must pass.
* Check with each channel PM that the signal is collected, respected and transmitted correctly.
**3. Monetization Under Privacy Constraints**
* Separate what is mandatory from what is only recommended, and measure the revenue impact of each option before a decision.
* Monetize traffic with no consent or partial consent: legitimate interest, contextual advertising, no-ad rules.
* Apply the rule “measure, decide, apply”: no traffic is rejected or degraded without a measurement and a written decision.
**4. Compliance, Vendors & Certifications**
* Own the IAB TCF and Google CMP certifications, and prevent any risk of deregistration.
* Manage the vendor list and custom vendors.
* Get each interpretation validated by our Data Protection Officer (DPO), who advises but does not decide.
**5. Privacy Point of Contact for Clients & Partners**
* Be the product contact for strategic clients and partners on privacy topics: CMP migrations, regulator requests, buyer requirements.
* Monitor upcoming regulations and standards, and turn them into roadmap items before they become urgent.
**6. Agentic Exposure & Cross-Functional Collaboration**
* Apply the agentic-first principle: every privacy rule and configuration must be executable by an AI agent, with clean data contracts and proper access controls.
* Work with Engagement (consent templates and A/B tests), UX Orchestration (CMP and paywall configuration), Analytics (signal measurement), FastCMP engineering and the DPO.

* **Technical Literacy:** You do not code, but you write specifications that engineers can apply without back-and-forth.
* **Data-Driven:** You measure before you decide: SQL basics, dashboards, A/B tests.

# **Principal Engineer, Data Quality Platform**
You'll own data correctness across Talos. You'll lead the data quality engineering team, run BAU data operations, and own reference and security master data, along with the pipelines and platform that deliver it.
Our goal: the data we return to clients is always correct, and we find defects before a client does.
You'll join a small team with the mandate to work independently from product engineering and challenge it. Engineering teams make assumptions about how their systems behave. Your job is to test those assumptions and prove or disprove them with evidence.
## Responsibilities
* Lead AI-first data quality engineering
* Validate every client-facing endpoint continuously. The focus is our REST and WebSocket APIs. Cloud delivery (S3, Snowflake, Databricks) is also in scope. Assert correctness against independent sources of truth, across every environment and client entitlement.
* Cover streaming as well as request/response. For WebSocket, that means:
* sequencing and gap detection
* snapshot-to-increment consistency
* reconnect and replay correctness
* staleness of live subscriptions
* agreement between the streamed view and the REST view of the same state
* Use adaptive detection, not static thresholds. Learn baselines per endpoint and per market, and let them adjust as "normal" changes. Hand-set limits get noisy, go stale, and teach people to ignore alerts.
* Apply LLM and agentic tooling to generate checks from API specs and schemas, keep them current as the product changes, and triage alerts before a human sees them. Know when a deterministic rule, invariant or cross-source reconciliation is the better tool.
* Test resilience and load. Design load, performance and failure-mode tests.
* When you find a fault, raise it with the owning team with enough evidence for them to act. Drive it to resolution, then add a check that would have caught it earlier.
* Measure and publish endpoint and field coverage, time to detect, detected-before-client rate and false-positive rate.
* Run data governance
* Build and maintain a catalog of our data assets and APIs, covering lineage and downstream consumers. Maintain an understanding of assets, how they're used and what breaks when they change.
* Own data governance tooling such as OpenMetadata.
* Own reference and security master data
* Lead the build-out of the next-generation security master platform, then run it day to day: new listings, symbol mapping across venues, and increment and contract specs.

* trade signals
* pre-trade analytics
* client post-trade analysis
* PMS analytics

* A deep understanding of streaming and API behaviour: throughput, WebSocket semantics, ordering, recovery and failure modes.
* Experience inventorying and testing a large API and data surface end to end.
* Hands-on experience with data governance: cataloging, lineage, ownership.
* Experience with performance and load testing of distributed systems.
* A strong engineering background. You design platforms, not scripts on a cron job, and you build on shared infrastructure rather than creating one-off tooling.
* Practical experience applying LLM and agentic tooling to engineering problems.
* Our stack: Flink, Doris, Dagster and Spark, plus OpenMetadata (or an equivalent such as Apache Atlas). Experience with comparable tools is just as relevant.

**Mission:**
TEKEVER's Regulations Manager holds overall responsibility for the regulatory and governance framework behind the company's flying activity, spanning both civil and defence contexts. The role is accountable for ensuring TEKEVER obtains and keeps in place the licences, authorisations and accreditations that let its uncrewed air systems (UAS) fly legally in the UK and in the other jurisdictions where TEKEVER operates.
Based within the Defence Division's Safety and Regulations team, the postholder produces SORA submissions and Operational Safety Cases for both civil and defence customers, runs several concurrent Operational Authorisation applications, and represents TEKEVER to a wide range of aviation regulators, among them the UK CAA, MAA, Ofcom, EASA, JARUS, Japan's JCAB and the US DoD, as well as other national aviation authorities as TEKEVER's international footprint grows. A working command of SORA BVLOS regulation underpins almost everything the role does.
##### Responsibilities
**Flight Operations Governance & Documentation**
• Own the suite of documents that govern how TEKEVER flies, among them OSC, OA, CFAOS and SORA, keeping them aligned to where the business needs to operate.
• Author and maintain SORA submissions and Operational Safety Cases on behalf of both civil and defence programmes.
• Prepare and lodge variations to existing SORAs, technical amendments and site-specific flying permissions as new requirements arise.
• Keep operational procedures, safety systems and supporting documentation compliant across every area of civil and defence flying.
**Regulatory Liaison, Approvals & Accreditation**
• Lead Operational Authorisation (OA) applications with National Aviation Authorities from first submission through to approval.
• Represent TEKEVER in dealings with aviation regulators, among them the UK CAA, MAA, EASA, JARUS, JCAB, the US DoD and other national authorities, whenever approvals, exemptions or authorisations are being sought.
• Support the business through accreditation under the Contractor Flying Approved Organisation Scheme (CFAOS) and, where needed, the Maintenance (MAOS) and Design (DAOS) Approved Organisation Schemes.
• Track the business's standing against MAA Regulatory Publications (MRP) so flying operations, safety management and operational readiness stay at the required level.
• Hold responsibility for TEKEVER's Ofcom spectrum permissions, watching expiry dates, lodging renewals ahead of time, and applying for coverage at new sites as they come online.
• Work with the design engineering team to pull together the technical data regulatory submissions depend on.
**Risk & Safety Management**
• Help run the Air Safety Management System (ASMS) so it meets NAA expectations.
• Contribute to hazard identification, risk assessment and mitigation planning as part of the wider risk management process.
• Monitor flight safety, airworthiness, airspace use and crew qualification practices in step with both internal procedure and external regulation.
• Support flight trials jointly with engineering and test teams so they run safely and under proper control.
• Make sure aviation activity across the business follows TEKEVER's Safety, Health & Environment (SHE) policies.
**Compliance Monitoring, Reporting & Continuous Improvement**
• Keep the business audit-ready for regulatory inspections, and close out any findings quickly.
• Work with the safety team to turn corrective actions around promptly and effectively.
• Report regularly on the status of regulatory applications and overall compliance.
• Track changes in national and international air legislation and update TEKEVER's documentation whenever the rules move.
• Put forward improvements to training, maintenance and flight operations practice.
• Push for continual improvement across safety culture, operational efficiency and the compliance process more broadly.
**Emergency Response & Advisory**
• Help put the Emergency Response Plan (ERP) into practice and keep it current.
• Act as the first port of call for colleagues with regulatory questions.
• Serve as the main point of contact, for both regulators and internal stakeholders, on accreditation and compliance matters.
##### Qualifications & Experience
**Essential**
• A track record of preparing and submitting SORA assessments, including applications in the UAS Specific Category, or equivalent regulatory process (crewed or uncrewed).
• Solid working knowledge of the UK's UAS regulatory landscape and the policy that underpins it.
• Familiarity with BVLOS operations and the rules that govern them.
• Able to communicate clearly, in writing and in person, within safety-critical and operational settings.
• Comfortable pulling together input from engineering, flight operations, flight test, safety and QA to get a submission over the line.
• Good analytical and problem-solving ability.
• Grounding in safety management principles and how they're applied day to day.
• Disciplined record-keeping: documentation and audit trails that hold up for both air systems and personnel.
• Comfortable representing the company to regulators, stakeholders and customers on aviation matters.
• Organised and safety-minded, with a bias toward getting ahead of problems.
• Degree-level education, or equivalent experience.
• Comfortable working in MS Teams and the wider MS Office suite.
**Desirable**
• A compliance monitoring qualification from the MAA, CAA or EASA.
• Background in civil and/or defence aviation or the wider aerospace sector.
• Experience juggling technical workstreams across several teams at once.
• Hands-on knowledge of UAS platforms: airframes, sensors, systems.
• Broad exposure to the regulatory frameworks that shape UK and international UAS operation, such as CAP 722, the MAA's MRP, OSC, SORA and SAIL.
• A good map of the regulatory landscape, UK and international bodies alike, from the MAA and CAA through to Ofcom, EASA, JARUS, JCAB and the US DoD.
• Comfort working with risk-based operating constructs such as SORA and PDRA.
• Some grounding in aircraft systems, maintenance needs and airworthiness paperwork.
• Awareness of how aviation safety management systems and incident reporting actually work in practice.
• A background in military aviation, maritime air operations, or a flight-operations/safety-culture role.
• Some knowledge of what flight training entails from a regulatory standpoint.
##### Security
• Candidates must be able to obtain SC clearance, which requires five years' continuous UK residency; TEKEVER will support applicants through that process.
##### Working Conditions
• Office-based in Bristol roughly two days a week, with the remainder spent on national and international travel (around 50% of the role).
• Regular travel to customer sites across the UK, Portugal, the US, wider EMEA and the Far East.
• Core hours apply, but evenings or weekends may be needed when operational urgency demands it.
##### Key Interfaces
• UK Civil Aviation Authority (CAA)
• Military Aviation Authority (MAA)
• Japan Civil Aviation Bureau (JCAB)
• Ofcom
• EASA and other international / foreign National Aviation Authorities (NAAs)
• JARUS
• Engineering, Flight Operations and Safety teams
• Air System and equipment design and production organisations

This includes a highly competitive salary with a discretionary annual bonus and a company pension contribution match of up to 10%. To support your wellbeing, we provide 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, Private Medical Insurance (with optional family cover), Private Dental care, and an Employee Assistance Programme. We are deeply committed to investing in future talent; our scale allows us to provide clear career development opportunities and dedicated initiatives to boost your skill sets, ensuring you remain future-ready for the evolving workplace. Furthermore, our team enjoys a flexible hybrid working model, typically three days a week at our core UK sites like Bristol, and access to a bespoke rewards platform featuring a variety of high street discounts and salary sacrifice schemes, including Electric Car, Cycle to Work, and Technology options.

# Senior Data Analyst – Enterprise Risk
## The role
Teya is building its Enterprise Risk Management Framework (ERMF) and strengthening how risk information is brought together, analysed and reported across the business.
As Senior Data Analyst, you will play a key role in turning risk data into reliable measures, meaningful insights and actionable reporting. You'll work closely with the Head of Enterprise & Operational Risk and stakeholders across Credit, Fraud, AML, People, IT, Operations and Finance to understand the risks facing the business, identify the right data to monitor them, and develop effective reporting and early-warning capabilities.
This is a business-facing analytical role. Understanding risk, working effectively with risk owners and translating their requirements into practical data solutions will be just as important as your technical skills. You'll help ensure key risk indicators (KRIs) are meaningful, data is reliable, thresholds are appropriately informed by analysis, and reporting supports better risk oversight and decision-making.
You'll also help modernise how risk reporting is produced, using AI models and workflow automation to bring together internal data and relevant external information, identify emerging issues and reduce manual effort. The focus is on practical application, with robust validation, traceability and human oversight.
This is an opportunity to combine risk expertise, analytical problem-solving and emerging AI capabilities to help shape how a growing fintech business identifies, monitors and manages risk.
## What you'll do
* **Develop risk data and reporting:** Identify and map relevant data sources, using tools such as Snowflake to build repeatable datasets for KRIs across operational, credit, fraud, AML, people, capital, liquidity and other risk categories.
* **Partner with risk stakeholders:** Work closely with the Head of Enterprise & Operational Risk and risk owners across the business to understand their priorities, clarify reporting requirements and translate risk management needs into practical analytical solutions.
* **Analyse and monitor risk indicators:** Use SQL and Python to investigate trends, test assumptions, identify anomalies and understand changes in risk exposure. Help risk owners interpret findings and determine where further investigation or action may be needed.
* **Support KRI definitions and thresholds:** Work with risk stakeholders to validate indicator definitions, assess data quality and analyse historical and current performance to inform threshold calibration. Help ensure indicators provide meaningful insight into the risks they are intended to monitor.
* **Build dashboards and management reporting:** Develop clear, accessible dashboards using Tableau, Power BI or similar tools, supporting monthly ERMF reporting and management oversight.
* **Automate risk reporting with AI:** Build and improve AI-enabled workflows that bring together internal data and relevant external signals, including regulatory updates, market developments, news and emerging threats. Help generate evidence-based reporting drafts for review by the Head of Enterprise & Operational Risk and CRO.
* **Develop early-warning capabilities:** Help design and test approaches to monitor KRI movements and operational data throughout the month, highlighting unusual patterns and potential emerging risks with clear supporting evidence for investigation.
* **Support risk technology and integration:** Translate ERMF and reporting requirements into practical data, integration and workflow specifications for Teya's governance, risk and compliance (GRC) solution, partnering with Risk, Data and Technology colleagues on implementation.
* **Improve data quality and governance:** Document data sources, definitions, lineage, refresh frequencies, validation checks and limitations to ensure reporting is consistent, explainable and reliable.
* **Drive continuous improvement:** Identify opportunities to simplify reporting, improve analytical processes and strengthen how risk information is used across the business.
## What you'll bring
* Experience in a data analytics, risk analytics or similar analytical role within a risk function, ideally covering enterprise, operational, credit, fraud or financial crime risk.
* A practical understanding of how risk is identified, assessed and monitored, including how risk appetite, controls, risk drivers, KRIs and thresholds connect.
* Strong business partnering skills, with the ability to work closely with risk owners and non-technical stakeholders, understand their needs and translate them into meaningful analysis, reporting and monitoring solutions.
* Working knowledge of SQL and Python for data analysis and practical automation. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be comfortable using these tools, including with AI assistance, and validating the accuracy of the results.
* Experience building dashboards and management reports using Tableau, Power BI or similar visualisation tools.
* Strong analytical judgement, with the ability to challenge assumptions, investigate unexpected results, assess data quality and communicate clearly what the data does—and does not—show.
* Experience working with data from multiple sources and improving the reliability, consistency and usability of analytical outputs.
* Hands-on curiosity about current AI models and AI-enabled workflow automation, with the ability to build and improve workflows that support data gathering, analysis and risk reporting.
* A structured, pragmatic approach to problem-solving, with the confidence to work through ambiguity and take ownership of deliverables.
## Useful, but not essential
* Experience in financial services, payments, fintech or another regulated environment.
* Exposure to enterprise risk management frameworks and risk appetite frameworks.
* Experience working with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.
* Familiarity with data pipelines, APIs, workflow orchestration or system integrations.
* Exposure to governance, risk and compliance (GRC) platforms.
* Experience with statistical analysis, anomaly detection, forecasting or early-warning indicators.
* Experience using external regulatory, market or threat intelligence to support risk monitoring.
* Familiarity with AI agents, large language models (LLMs) or AI-enabled workflow automation tools.
## What success looks like
* **Trusted risk data:** KRI datasets are accurate, consistent, well-documented and refreshed at the required frequency.
* **Meaningful risk insight:** Analysis helps risk owners understand changes in risk exposure, investigate anomalies and make informed decisions.
* **Effective business partnering:** Risk stakeholders have confidence in the data, reporting and analysis provided, and their requirements are translated into practical solutions.
* **Clear management reporting:** Monthly ERMF reporting is timely, evidence-based and increasingly automated.
* **Earlier identification of emerging risks:** Explainable monitoring highlights significant movements and potential issues for investigation.
* **Reliable AI-enabled workflows:** Automation reduces manual effort while maintaining accuracy, traceability and appropriate human review.
* **Stronger risk data foundations:** Data definitions, quality checks and reporting processes support the continued development of Teya's ERMF and GRC capabilities.
## Benefits
* **Competitive salary:** A competitive package aligned with your experience and impact.
* **Equity participation:** The opportunity to share in Teya's growth, subject to the applicable scheme and eligibility.
* **Pension:** Workplace pension provision.
* **Holiday:** Generous annual leave to support a healthy work-life balance.
* **Flexible working:** A flexible working environment built around collaboration, ownership and getting things done.
* **Learning and development:** Opportunities to develop your risk, data analytics and AI automation skills as the business grows.
* **Health and wellbeing:** Support for your wellbeing, with benefits designed to help you thrive at work and beyond.
* **Team and company events:** Opportunities to connect with colleagues, share ideas and celebrate success.

# **Residential Facilities Manager**
## **Purpose of Role**
At The Crown Estate, we take a long-term approach to creating value and positive outcomes for the people, places and environments connected to our portfolio.
As 'Residential Facilities Manager', you will deliver high-quality facilities management across our residential portfolio. You will help ensure our buildings and communal areas are safe, compliant and maintained to a consistently high standard, supporting an excellent experience for residents.
Working collaboratively with Property Managers, Block Managers, Hard Services colleagues and the wider Portfolio Operations team, you will oversee day-to-day hard and soft services. This includes maintenance, contractor performance, statutory compliance, operational risk and service charge management. You will also act as a key point of contact for service partners and internal stakeholders.

This is an opportunity to play an important role in the effective operation of a diverse residential and mixed-use portfolio. You will combine hands-on facilities management with strong stakeholder relationships, ensuring services are responsive, well controlled and aligned with our commitment to responsible stewardship.

* Delivering day-to-day facilities management across residential assets, ensuring buildings are safe, compliant and well maintained.

* Maintaining effective emergency and incident-response arrangements, including out-of-hours readiness.
* Working with Property Managers and Block Managers to align operational delivery with asset plans and identify emerging risks, issues and opportunities.
* Maintaining statutory, regulatory, health and safety, fire safety and building safety compliance.

* Proven facilities management experience within a residential or mixed-use environment.

## Job Description
Guardian News & Media (GNM) is a leading global media organisation, publisher of the guardian.com and The Guardian newspaper, acclaimed for investigative journalism on topics such as phone hacking among the UK press, the Paradise Papers and Panama Papers, the Pegasus Project and investigations into Nigel Farage and his finances. As well as being the UK’s largest quality news brand, GNM has pioneered a highly distinctive, open approach to publishing on the web and has achieved significant global audience growth over the past 20 years, with growing newsrooms and operations in the US and Australia
Guardian News and & Media operates a system of self-regulation that consists of editorial standards and behaviour governed by the GNM editorial code of practice, an internally independent readers’ editor who receives complaints from readers who believe that journalists have breached the GNM editorial code of practice, and an independent review panel established in 2014 by the Scott Trust.
The review panel exists to ensure that where complainants do not feel their issues have been adequately resolved through the internal complaints procedures, they have the chance to have their complaint further considered by an independent panel. The role of the review panel is to consider only those complaints that fall under one of the 16 sections of the revised GNM editorial code of practice Editors’ Code of Practice. Its role is not to regulate GNM, or its journalists or to review complaints against wider guidance to GNM journalists.
The Scott Trust is responsible for appointing the review panel. **The Trust is seeking to appoint a new member of its review panel**to work alongside existing chair and panel members to assess complaints received by the panel, in accordance with its terms of reference. The successful candidate is likely to have an understanding of digital journalism and media regulation. **Person specification**
**Candidates must be able to demonstrate the following essential criteria:**
* The capacity to act fairly and impartially in the decision-making of the panel.
* Knowledge and experience of the process of journalism or news publishing.
* Experience of the role of self-regulation in maintaining high standards of industry practice. Knowledge of media law would be welcome.
* An understanding of journalistic codes of practice, processes and standards.
* An affinity with The Scott Trust values of honesty, integrity, courage, fairness, a sense of duty to the reader and the community and public interest journalism.
**Responsibilities:**
* To consider and scrutinise case bundles provided to the review panel with a view to playing an active role in helping the panel to make a determination.
* To work collegiately with other panel members to come to a consensus view on the outcomes of cases.
**Appointment Term**
New panel members will be appointed for an initial term of four years, which may be extended once by a further period of four years.
**Time Commitment**
The panel is expected to meet at least quarterly, however, the panel may meet more or less frequently depending on the demands of caseload. When and how the panel meets will ultimately be at the discretion of the panel Chair and its members.
**Remuneration**
Successful applicants are paid £5,000 pa.
**How to apply?**
Please send your CV together with a covering letter of no more than two pages, with examples of how you meet our selection criteria.
**The closing date for applications is 6pm, Sunday 15th November 2026.**

* Manage and maintain project information, drawings and resources.
* Ensure high standards of workmanship by monitoring projects closely.
* Identify and act to mitigate risks throughout the project lifecycle.

About the Role
We're looking for a software engineer to build the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. You'll design a manifest-driven API where the inference team declares what they need, whether that's a cluster, a model deployment, or a capacity change, and our controllers handle the reconciliation, provider/runtime selection, and lifecycle management underneath, so the inference team never has to know or care which specific serving stack, scheduler, or hardware pool is doing the work. You'll also build the systems that keep the fleet efficient, not just running, including defragmentation and rebalancing logic that consolidates scattered workloads back into contiguous capacity, and scheduling/bin-packing improvements that push GPU utilization up without hurting latency. The core value we're after is decoupling the people building on top of the platform from the operational and runtime complexity underneath, while squeezing more usable capacity out of the same hardware. You'll build the controllers, reconciliation loops, and self-service surface (API/CLI, not tickets) that make that decoupling real, plus the event-driven health, remediation, and utilization systems that keep it running and efficient without a human in the loop. Strong candidates have hands-on experience with Kubernetes controller/CRD patterns, have built or operated a platform API that abstracts multiple backends behind one interface, understand GPU scheduling and capacity efficiency (fragmentation, bin-packing, right-sizing), and think about GPU infrastructure as software to be engineered.
A product mindset - you've built internal platforms or APIs consumed by other engineering teams and care about the developer experience of what you ship.You build it, you own it. You are not only responsible for delivering the software but also for operating and supporting it in production.
Responsibilities
Build the provisioning state machine: design and implement the software that models the full lifecycle of a physical host from discovery, inference bring-up to GPU driver/CUDA stack, health validation, and decommission/RMA — as explicit, versioned states and transitions.
Build the self-service API: design declarative APIs and a control plane so the inference team can request, scale, and tear down inference clusters with one API call — no ticket, no human in the loop.
Automate self-healing: detect degraded or failed nodes, drain them safely, trigger repair or replacement, and reintroduce healthy capacity into the pool automatically.
Own reliability of the pipeline: idempotency, retries, rollback, and drift detection so the provisioning system is as dependable as any other production service.
Partner with the inference/ML platform team: understand the cluster shapes they need — topology, interconnect, scheduling constraints — and encode them as first-class abstractions in the platform.
Engineer it like software: strong typing, automated tests, code review, versioning, and CI/CD for infrastructure code — this is a product, not a collection of Ansible playbooks.
Requirements
Core requirements (all levels):
Strong software engineering background in Go, Python, Rust, or similar — you write and test real software for a living.
Experience with durable workflow orchestration tools such as Temporal, Cadence, or equivalent to run long-lived, manifest-driven workflows that survive failures and resume mid-execution.
Experience building software control planes or orchestration systems that model state and reconcile it over time (e.g., Kubernetes controllers/operators, custom reconciliation loops, workflow engines).
Experience with event-driven systems — designing and building software around message queues, event streams, or pub/sub (e.g., Kafka, NATS, SQS) rather than polling or cron-driven scripts.
A product mindset. You’ve built internal platforms or APIs consumed by other engineering teams and care about the developer experience of what you ship.
Nice to have:
Exposure to bare-metal provisioning (PXE/iPXE, Redfish/IPMI, BMC) and/or networking fundamentals (VLANs, BGP, fabric design), or GPU/accelerator infrastructure.
Experience with GPU cluster software stacks (NCCL, CUDA, InfiniBand/RoCE).
Prior work at a hyperscaler, GPU cloud, or datacenter-scale infrastructure organization.
Systems programming in Rust or Go.

# Senior Brand Manager
## Own brand campaigns, product innovation and packaging at TRIP, turning consumer insight into standout launches and shaping the next chapter of a fast-growing global wellness brand.
##### **Senior Brand Manager - TRIP**
##### **Location: Notting Hill, London — four days in the office and one from home Reporting to: Head of Brand**
##### **ABOUT TRIP:**
TRIP’s mission is to create calm in the everyday chaos for our community, offering next-generation wellness products to power their lifestyle and nurture mental wellbeing.
Co-founders, husband-and-wife team Olivia and Daniel, discovered plant-based wellness after a transformative personal experience and launched TRIP in 2019 to bring delicious, high-quality functional drinks and supplements to millions of people globally.
Now the world’s #1 Calming Beverage Brand, TRIP’s award-winning drinks and wellness products are crafted with botanicals and adaptogens to help people relax, unwind and find balance. Since launch, TRIP has rapidly expanded from the UK across Europe and North America, generating over $100 million in sales. Our products are available in leading supermarkets, natural retailers and online.
Our vision is to become the global leader in calming drinks and supplements — synonymous with calm in the same way Red Bull is with energy. We move fast, think big and are committed to becoming the defining brand for a generation who drinks less but prioritises mental wellbeing more than ever.
There has never been a better time to join our team and be part of the movement.
##### THE ROLE
We're looking for an ambitious, commercially minded Senior Brand Manager to help shape the next chapter of TRIP's growth.
This is an exciting opportunity to take ownership across three critical areas of our business: Brand Marketing, Product Innovation and Packaging. You'll play a key role in bringing our brand to life, launching exciting new products and ensuring TRIP shows up consistently and brilliantly wherever consumers discover us.
Working closely with our Brand, Digital, Sales, Social, Partnerships and Product teams, you'll turn consumer insights and commercial opportunities into impactful campaigns, compelling products and standout packaging.
We're looking for someone who combines strategic thinking with a hands-on, can-do attitude. Someone who's as comfortable developing a brand campaign as they are managing a product launch, challenging a creative brief or getting into the detail to make things happen.
You'll be joining an ambitious, fast-growing business where you'll have genuine ownership, creative freedom and the opportunity to make a visible impact on a globally recognised brand.
##### WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
**Brand Strategy & Campaigns**
* **Lead integrated brand campaigns:** Take ownership as the Brand lead for alternating 360° brand and new product development (NPD) campaigns, working collaboratively with our Digital, Sales, Social and Partnerships teams to deliver impactful activations.
* **Bring our brand strategy to life:** Develop clear, inspiring and actionable campaign briefs that translate our wider brand strategy into a consistent direction for creative execution across teams and channels.
* **Drive campaign effectiveness:** Monitor campaign performance across channels, bringing together insights and results to evaluate impact, identify opportunities and make informed recommendations for future brand investment.
* **Champion brand consistency:** Act as a guardian of TRIP's brand identity, ensuring our visual identity, tone of voice and brand guidelines are consistently reflected across every consumer and product touchpoint.
* **Evolve our brand expression:** Lead bi-annual reviews of brand execution across product touchpoints, identifying opportunities to strengthen consistency, relevance and impact as TRIP continues to grow.
* **Support commercial growth:** Develop compelling brand and product sell-in materials that help our Sales teams communicate the TRIP proposition, build excitement with retail partners and champion our product range.
##### Product Innovation & Portfolio Development
* **Shape the future of our portfolio:** Support the development of TRIP's product range architecture and innovation roadmap, balancing exciting new opportunities with the performance and growth of our existing core range.
* **Lead the brand side of innovation:** Partner closely with our Product team to shape and deliver the NPD pipeline, using consumer insights, market trends and commercial opportunities to inform product concepts, focus areas and flavour development.
* **Turn ideas into products:** Develop detailed, insight-led product briefs covering flavour profiles, functional benefits, product formats, pricing and target consumers, ensuring innovation is aligned with our brand positioning and commercial objectives.
* **Own the journey to launch:** Manage NPD timelines, cross-functional milestones and implementation plans, keeping teams aligned and ensuring new products are delivered successfully and on schedule.
* **Optimise portfolio performance:** Track and analyse product performance to support informed decisions around future innovation, product optimisation, portfolio priorities and potential delistings.
##### Packaging & Brand Execution
* **Lead packaging development:** Oversee the evolution of TRIP's packaging across our drinks and supplements portfolio, including cans, multipacks and point-of-sale materials, managing projects from initial concept and creative brief through to final delivery on shelf.
* **Manage the creative and artwork process:** Project manage packaging artwork workflows and coordinate the packaging team, ensuring all designs are delivered accurately, on time and in line with TRIP's brand guidelines.
* **Ensure regulatory compliance:** Work closely with Compliance and relevant internal teams to ensure all packaging meets applicable UK, US and EU regulatory requirements, including product claims, ingredient declarations and nutritional information.
* **Keep launches on track:** Own packaging-related critical paths, coordinating internal stakeholders and external partners to manage deadlines, resolve challenges and ensure launches land on time and within budget.
* **Balance creativity with execution:** Ensure packaging is visually distinctive, commercially effective and practical to deliver, maintaining the quality and consistency consumers expect from TRIP.
##### WHAT YOU'LL BRING
##### Desired Experience & Skills
* **Strong brand management experience:** Ideally 5+ years' experience in brand marketing, with experience operating at Brand Manager or Senior Brand Manager level within an FMCG or consumer goods environment.
* **Relevant category experience:** A background in food, beverages, functional drinks, wellness, beauty or other fast-moving consumer brands would be particularly valuable.
* **End-to-end campaign management:** Proven experience developing and delivering integrated brand campaigns, from initial strategy and briefing through to execution, measurement and post-campaign evaluation.

Kenyon has been there when it matters most for 120 years. We support more than 500 organisations across aerospace, government, events, maritime and energy with a network of over 2,500 specialist responders.
